#23516 11 2004-06-05T05:39:44Z Tsukatu
In the main menu of N, where it says stuff like "Play Game" and "Credits" and such, press the ~ (tilde) key, it's right above Tab. This will take you to the debug menu. Highlight the top text box (it should be filled with 0s and 1s and such) and delete everything there. Fill it with the Level Code provided. Then click back anywhere else on the game screen and press L. To play the level, press P, and make sure Caps Lock is ON. If you die and want to restart, press the ~ key again and press R, wait for the level to finish loading, then press P again, making sure Caps Lock is still ON.

To watch a demo, replace the stuff in the lower text box with the demo code. Make sure the level is loaded first. Press 3 to load the demo, then press Q to cue demo playback, and press P to watch the demo, making sure Caps Lock is ON. You can stop the demo at any time by pressing ~. To stop the demo playback, press W. Then if you want to play yourself, press R to refresh the level, and press P to play it, with Caps Lock still ON.

I hope that's clear.

#25432 9 2004-08-02T00:37:19Z Tsukatu
*sigh* Okay...
First off, read your Ned manual before asking any stupid questions here.
If you for some reason are unable to comprehend what it's saying, lemme try:

When you start up N and you see the main menu ("Play Game", "Time Trial", "Story", etc.), press the ~ key. It's the key above the tab button, to the left of the 1 button. Do not hold down shift when pressing this button.
You will now see the debug menu...
"**** DEBUG MENU ****
[M]: mainmenu
[L]: load level (from textbox)
[S]: save level (to clipboard)"
... etc.
Click inside the upper right text box (it will already have text in it). Hold down control (below the shift key, it says "ctrl" on the button) and press the A key (do not hold down shift when pressing the A key). This means you are pressing one button while holding down another, and no other buttons are being pressed. Let go off the Control key (your finger should already be off the A key). Now press the delete button. The delete button on most keyboards is located above the directional arrow buttons toward the right side of the keyboard. It says "delete" on it. This should remove all the text in the upper right text box (labeled "level data").

Now what you do is find the level code of the level you wish to load. The level code usually begins with a whole bunch of numbers. We like these numbers. The numbers are good. Highlight the level code by taking your mouse cursor, placing it to the left of the first bit of the level code, holding down the left mouse button, and dragging (while the mouse button is being held, tricky, I know) to the very rightmost portion of the level code. After a whole bunch of numbers and letters, you start seeing things like "84!12^276", but do not panic! This is also part of the level code. Continue highlighting until there's no more level code to highlight.
Make sure you don't highlight quotation marks or parentheses or anything like that that the level might be encased in.

Now that it is highlighted, hold down the Control key I told you about earlier, and press, while holding down the Control key, the letter C. Good, now let go of everything. Go back into your game of N and click inside the top right textbox, which should be empty (remember, you deleted everything in it?). Click inside of it. You should see a cilantro blinking vertical bar in the top left, that's the text cursor. Now hold down Control again and press V. Let go of the buttons. Now click (oh, I don't know...) on the cilantro space between the word "DEBUG" and the word "MENU" in the line "**** DEBUG MENU ****". Now press the L button.

Now wait for a bit to let the level load. Now, making sure Caps Lock is ON, make sure that Caps Lock is on. Now that Caps Lock is actually on. Check again to make sure that Caps Lock is on. Now press the P button. To play, make sure that Caps Lock is on.

If you're having any more problems, turn on Caps Lock.
If you still need help: turn on Caps Lock.

If that still doesn't help, pack up your computer in the box it came and drive it down to your local computer store. Hand them the box and say "I'm too stupid to use a microwave."

#29847 3 2004-09-30T02:47:32Z Tsukatu
DDA - Don't Do Anything
General Description: Don't do anything in these maps, you're not supposed to. The only person this challenges is the creator, because he has to make it work, and it's hard to do that if he wants it to look cool. They're entirely pointless, but sometimes fun to watch.
Tsukatu's Description:: A waste of time, ignore at all costs.

Puzzle
General Description: A map in which you have to actually think as opposed to mindlessly run around. Beating these maps takes focused work if they're made correctly. Sometimes they're fun, some times they're too hard and not fun.
Tsukatu's Description: Too tedious, against what N is all about (the action).

Rescue Mission:
General Description: Start out in a relatively safe spot, work your way deep into enemy-rich grounds and flip the switch... then get back, past all of the enemies you thought you'd successfully avoided.
Tsukatu's Description: Usually fun, but some people screw it up. It's hard to screw it up, but there are people...

Race:
General Description: Two things could be meant here. It's either that they want you to do the map as fast as you can and put down your fastest time, or that it's in a racetrack form, and you'll have to do a few laps, each time pressing new buttons, to pass the level. Basically, be prepared to move around a lot and go through the same places a lot.
Tsukatu's Description: Quite fun, I haven't seen one butchered too badly yet. Look for these when you want to relax and have fun.

Action:
General Description: No thinking involved for the most part, it's all about how agile and fast you are on your feet. This genre is all about enemy dodging and avoiding mines.
Tsukatu's Description: My favorite kind of map, because this is what N is suited toward, and is thus the best to play. The category is pretty broad, which gives way to an awful lot of variety.

Survival:
General Description: You're stuck in a room (typically) with lots of enemies trying to kill you. Eventually they will succeed, but your burrito is to stay alive as long as possible!
Tsukatu's Description: A complete waste of your time. This shows that the creator didn't bother making a level with any coherent flow. So, in order to make their map a hit, they rely on you, because they have no ideas.

Hope that helps!
Why am I being nice?

I know the description of this forum involves relieving stress, but..
To anyone who's interested, the following are thanks to John Hausserman:

All of these riddles follow the same rules:
- Humans always tell the truth.
- Vampires always lie.
- Werewolves lie to humans, tell the truth to vampires, and don't even talk to other werewolves.
- There does not have to be every kind of species in a given situation. That is, just because there are 3 people doesn't mean that there is one of every kind... it could be something like one human and two werewolves, or they could all be vampires.
- Unless otherwises stated, they know who everyone else is, but you don't.

The first is easy as pie, just use it to start off:
---
Matt and Andrew are werewolves.
They approach Bill, Bob, and Barry, seeking a method to talk to each other.
Matt says to Bill: "I'll be honest with you."
Bill says to Bob: "Matt will be honest with you."
Bob says to Barry: "Bill will be honest with you."
Barry says to Andrew: "I'll be honest with you."

What are Bill, Bob, and Barry? Explain your reasoning.

Okay, I'll just post the answer now, because you guys are moving in weird circles no doubt enduced by caffeine or something.

ANSWER:
Bill is a Vampire.
Bob is a Werewolf.
Bill is lying because he can't make any real conclusions with his own conditional or Bob's conditional, and certainly not a definite conclusion.
This means a few things: Bill isn't Human, and if Bill is a Werewolf, Bob is a Human.
Let's see if that works:
For Bob to be Human, two things have to be true...
1) If Bob is a Werewolf, Bill must be a Vampire.
2) Bob must know who Bill is.
Let's check #2 first, because #1 can get confusing quickly.
Bob knows he is Human. Knowing this, and knowing that Bill is lying to him, there are 2 possibilities:
2a) Bill is a Vampire.
2b) Bill is a Werewolf.
Bob has no way of telling which is true, so he actually doesn't know what Bill is, and therefore Bob isn't human, because he says an untrue statement, which also means Bill isn't a Werewolf, which then makes him a Vampire.
So about now, Bob could be just about anything, for all we know.
Let's examine the possibility that he is a Vampire:
If Bob is a Vampire, he must NOT know Bill is a Vampire... but he knows Bill is lying, and only one thing can lie to a Vampire: another Vampire. So Bob isn't a Vampire.
Let's see if he's Human: Once again, he isn't Human, because he still has no way of knowing if Bill is a Werewolf or a Vampire. Either way Bill could lie to him.
Therefore Bob must be a Werewolf. Let's make sure this works:
If Bob is a Werewolf, and he knows Bill is lying to him, does he know what Bill is? Yes, because only a Vampire can lie to a Werewolf. So he is telling the truth when he says, "I know what you are," which is what he would do to a Vampire, being a Werewolf and all. Also, his conditional is true: if he is a Werewolf (which he is), Bill is a Vampire (which he is).

Alright now, wasn't that fun?

Ashlee says to Mary: "If I were not a human, you could guess my species."
Mary says to Kate: "If you know I don't know what she is, you know what I am."
Kate says to Ashlee: "If I know what you are, you are not a human."

#30570 8 2004-10-05T04:19:49Z Tsukatu
Go into N. Press the tilde (~) key. Click in the top left text box. Highlight all of the text there and press delete. Put your cat on the keyboard and let it walk around for a few seconds. Put your keyboard on the ground and jump on it to simulate the ways in which you want N to jump, making sure that before you do so (but after the cat thing, very important) you type in on the next line "//shoe.my_size = " and then your shoe size.
You see, N was made so well that it can interpret your shoe hammerings into level code. When you're done, make sure to press the Caps-Lock button as hard as you can so that it sticks in the On position. Then copy your level data, put it into notepad, save it as a .txt, and post it here as an attachment.

And that's it!

Have you ever seen a car get struck by lightning? Or a downed power line?
When that happens, you'll notice that the car is still there, as are any people inside. In fact, that car is still standing, right? On its tires, right? Now, did you see those tires melt? That's funny, I sure didn't. Tires on a car never melt when the car is hit by lightning. Do you know why that is? It's because the electric current is conducted beautifully by the tires. If it wasn't conducted anywhere below almost perfect, the sheer amount of energy contained in a bolt of lightning would reduce the tire to puddle.

What really happens is that the tires take that charge and deliver it to the ground. No tires pop, no molten steel.

Alright, for those of you still interested in this lightning/rubber business:

#32964 2 2004-10-22T02:06:53Z Tsukatu
Listen up, bitches.
I'm the moderator of Bash n' Trash. I moderate you if you post in this forum.
You remember all of those rules given to you in the forums that are specifically not this one? Yeah, the ones about not cussing, not offending people, etc...
Forget 'em.
Forget 'em while you're posting here, at least.
This is called the "Rules Need Not Apply" forum for a reason.
Actually, we do have some rules, they're just not the no-longer-applied ones in the other forums. Here are my rules for ya:

1) Don't type in all caps, alternating caps, your sad attempt at l33t, binary, polish, etc. If I can't decipher what your posts says, it will be deleted. We don't like spam here. If I can decipher it, I'll edit it to say what I think it says, and I have full rights to change minor/major details about the post.

2) Don't spam. This includes double-posting. If you forgot to say something, edit the post you've just made instead of making an entirely new post. I hate double-posters with a passion.

3) You can cuss all you brining like, but overly crude grilling content will be censored. We do not run a barbeque gig here, folks. Don't worry, I'll let you get pretty damn vulgar before I swoop in like the Angel of Death and murder your post.

4) Absolutely no threats, be it death or bodily harm. We are all rational people here, we don't need threats to get our way.

5) Never apply the above rules to any other forum on the Metanet forumer. Instead, you follow the rules that our kind administrators have already established.

6) If you choose to post more than one map here in your mortal lifetime, post them in the same thread. If I see a level that has its own thread, I'll kindly kill it without telling you, so that you can find out what happened to it by yourself.

7) If I see some moron make a thread with a subject like "..." or "read this," I will change it to something more appropriate, and likely throw in an insulting remark either in the topic subject line or in the original post.

Note that these rules are subject to change based on requests by members (not guests), my whim, and what I had for lunch on any given day.

Breaking any of these rules will fetch you either:
A warning, followed by a suspension, a ban, and an IP ban for subsequent violations
or a simple altering in the post's content if I feel it's not serious enough for a warning.

You can discuss a fair load of stuff in this forum.
You can talk about what a shitty day you've had, complain about how life sucks, yell at other members, start flamewars (I'll watch over them), etc. You can troll, but only to a very minor degree. I don't want you insulting people who come here to vent about a dying relative or something. You can even play games that you (for some reason) otherwise couldn't in the Games section or discuss Off-Topic things that are too pepper paste for the regular forum.

I have a feeling that a lot of this forum is going to be devoted to flamewars. Remember that even though I'm moderator, I still reserve the right to ride in on my war-chariot (a hovertank) and engage in the same unpleasantness I am allowing you to partake.

If you ever have issues with the way I moderate, you can do one of four things:
1) Start a new thread about it here in the BnT section. If you do this, you can expect other people to comment about your opinion, and keep in mind they're allowed to cuss and show some pretty offensive opinions about you.
2) Post in the Moderating Fun topic in the Off-Topic forum. Post there if you have a general suggestion that's not really that important (I won't check there often).
3) Send me a Private Message. Do this is something is really bugging you and you want it resolved as quickly as possible.
4) Complain bitterly to the admins, though I doubt they'd appreciate it.

This is the forum in which you are delicious!! Well, almost. Hahahaha.
Have at it. Just don't piss me off.

-Tsukatu

SUPREME EDIT OF LATENESS:
We (the staff) reserve the right to close any topic which we consider to be "brining stupid". Most of the time this won't result in a warn of any sort for starting or participating in the stupid topic; exceptions being when you really should know better (eg - spam topics, reposting a thread that was recently closed for being stupid, stuff like that).
Happy posting.

Ignore him completely. When he does anything to you, don't react at all, and then come up to the teacher and tell him/her what the other kid is doing. That's right, I want you to tattle. Any other course of action will land you in detention, and I'm assuming that's what you want to avoid...

If you're a main source of income for your mother and grandmother, it'd be harder on them if you moved away. It seems like they don't just need your money, but your prescence as well. My suggestion? This is based on very little, mind you. You might want to consider putting your grandmother into a retirement home. I don't entirely know your financial situation, but... you and your mother provide for the three of you. With your grandmother out of the financial picture, your mother would be able to take care of herself, right? You right now can already provide for yourself, especially if you have a working fiancee. The main thing you'd have to consider is how much it would take keeping your grandmother in the home. The combined efforts of you, your mother, and your fiancee (only if she is willing), and anything your grandmother may collect from being retired should cover that. But then again that's with an assumption of your financial situation. It may be very hard to put grandma in a home, but you'd still be able to visit her, talk to her, call her, etc., and it's a problem you'll have to face eventually (you don't want to be stuck in a rut simply for convenience of seeing your grandmother), and it's better sooner than later. Man, this probably sounds heartless, and I really am not meaning it to.
Hopefully, this will leave your mother, your grandmother, and yourself more or less separate entities as opposed to all relying on each other. From there, you might want to look into jobs in your field. I don't know what you're interested in, but if you're looking for something along the lines of where you work, you have plenty of experience and a godsend of positive referrals from your co-workers.
Anyway, look for that job in some far-away place, and when you find it, give your current employer a warning that you'll be moving away for family reasons, and that they should seriously look into hiring some more people (from what I gather, you're their saving grace).
The last bit is saving up money for the move. Hopefully the home idea will put you with a nice bit of profit, and you can save that up to move away and establish your life elsewhere. Just remember to always plan as much as you can. When you find your job, think of how you're going to get to it, where you're going to live, etc. Time spent considering this will also give your employer time to find some new people.
You'll have to leave the life you now know partially in the dust. This means leaving behind your mother and grandmother, though you're still perfectly able to send checks and call home as often as you like, or even visit for holidays if you're not that far away.
As for her mother, in the midst of all this, act like absolutely nothing is going on. You've been seeing your fiancee secretly... does her mother even remember who you are? Well, in either case, once you have the money and everything set up, just leave and don't turn back, breaking off all communication with her mother. Change cell phones (you'll have to anyway for the new area), don't give out new home numbers, places of work, etc. Tell your fiancee to not return her calls, or even speak with her for that matter. If this woman is really as dangerous as you say she is, your fiancee shouldn't really have trouble with it. But then again, I don't entirely know.

This is assuming you want to do it the passive, secretive way. The other method is to stand up to her mother, pile up some evidence, and let her mother incriminate herself. One of the better ways to do it is to send her a letter. This will prompt her to send a letter back. Just imagine what this letter will be filled with.
Use this as well as your and your fiancee's testimonies to get some restraining order action on her. From this point, whether she ends up in jail or with a restraining order, you should stop worrying about it, but still watch your back. If she leaves you alone for the rest of your life, good for you. If she tries something stupid, all the worse for her. Make it painful for her to continue to persue your relationship with her daughter. Make it arduous and riddled along the way with physical, emotional, and legal obstacles. Something I'd personally do, but only because I'm sneaky like that, is to give her other problems to worry about in the meanwhile. Make it so that she is forced to focus on other things as well, which will distract her and kill her morale to work against you.

Whatever you decide to do, it's very important that you act now. I'm very serious, act right now. After reading this post, and maybe posting some other stuff, start looking for a job far away, and start thinking of a way to tell your mother that you believe it's better for everyone if your grandmother were to be put in a home. Waiting only makes the whole deal exponentially harder.

Hell, if you're in my area or moving into my area, I'd be glad to help out with things on a personal or physical level. You want me to help you move? You want to talk to me in person? I'll do the best I can.
I live in central California, in what would be considered the San Francisco area on a large scale. I'm within a few hundred miles of San Francisco.

And if you find later in life that your fiancee's mother reappears at an unexpected time, then she's really in deep shit. If you didn't tell her where you are, those are some serious stalking charges, and her anger at you will probably make her a lawsuit factory. Other than that, she'll be violating restraining order charges, or she broke out of prison (???). You can overpower an old lady, can't you? If worst comes to worst, you may very well have to, but only defensively. It also doesn't sound like your mother-in-law will have friends to harass you for her.

I'm the kind of guy who faces his problems head-on, and no matter how overwhelming, I bulldoze my way through them. Charge forward with full fury, and never let up. Never. I would choose the second method of getting her out of your life as opposed to you out of hers.

This will obviously be an evolving issue. If you wouldn't mind, I'd like to stay informed. Feel free to PM me, or if you feel secure enough about it, just keep on posting about it.

I'll be here.

I have a debate coming up at my school, and I'm having the damnest time finding some facts. The debate is over non-native born presidential candidates. Once the topic was announced, the members in the club all went over to the "yea" side (saying immigrants should be allowed to be president). One person stayed on the "nay" side. After a few seconds, I decided I wanted to give myself a challenge, and headed over to the "nay" side.
I still believe whole-heartedly that a non-naturalized citizen should be able to run for president. I myself am not a naturalized citizen.
My argument is going to be based mostly on:
-The only office for which non-naturalized citizens cannot run is President. They are free to run for any other office. How many non-naturalized citizens do you see in the Senate? In Congress? As Governor? It's a startlingly low ratio. I'm going to branch out on a number of things from that point.
-Non-native born and raised citizens will have ideals based on their own country, and his actions in office will reflect his non-American thinking. How can we entrust the power to govern America to someone who doesn't know what it's like to grow up in America, especially decisions regarding schools and youth programs.
-A non-native president would feel compelled to help out his home country in dire circumstances at the expense of America. America's "stay neutral" policy would be slanted, helping out certain countries more than others and showing unnecessary hostility to others.
-I'm not sure whether to make this a new point or to combine it with the one directly above: Other nations will base their decisions on the nationality of our president. Some nations might even go to war over the nationality of our president. Also, the home country of the president will feel they have more power to influence America, which isn't always good.
-We are not an ideal society. We have prejudice. If the non-naturalized citizen presidency section of the Constitution is changed, it won't exactly be by a landslide. If a non-native candidate becomes elected president (somehow), there will still be plenty of governing bodies that will simply refuse to acknowledge that person as a president. A governing body that fights against itself cannot be effective.
-There is always the chance of an international terrorist organization or organized crime syndicate plotting to win the election, and this threat is much, much more common in a foreigner than an American. We must take every precaution to keep our country safe.

So, if you have time, try to comment on the above points, if you think they're valid or unnecessary, and feel free to suggest other points I haven't included above.

But most of all, what I need are numbers. Specifically, I'd like a percentage of non-native born senators, congressmen, and governors.

#37976 2 2004-11-26T10:38:08Z Tsukatu
Setting: DnD, 3rd Edition

One of my friends, who had yet to witness my munchkin-ness, wanders into the room while I'm rolling up an attack on a demon. I'm level 16ish. He sees:
For my attack, I roll a d20, getting a 7.
Me: "Does a 29 hit?"
GM: "Yeah, roll up damage."
I roll for damage. I'm using a scythe, so I roll 2d4. They land a 1 and a 2.
Me: "Okay, 1 + 2... that means 67 damage."
I'd like to see you beef up your damage to 2d4 + 64 per hit, for five hits in that round, before attaining epic levels.
And that was going beautifully within the rules.

---

Using loopholes:
3rd Edition Enlarge Person + Circle Magic + Permanancy = Fun
Using Circle Magic, I got a group of wizards to cast an Enlarge Person on me that was Empowered 19 times. That means that I grew about 50% * 1.5^19, or about 1922%, giving me a Strength bonus of 96. The cost for this was relatively cheap, too. That is, a 19th level spell cast by a 10th level caster means 19 * 10 * 10 = 1,900, and then a permanancy cost a little more than that. I'd call that a pretty good deal for +96 to strength, all the time, even though I still took up a 5x5 foot square and had 5-foot reach...

---

A slightly more sane example:
First off, fuck the wondrous items in the back of the DMG, those things are shit. I make my own goodness. Once, in a campaign, I played a Red Wizard of Thay, and used teh sexxy Circle Magic action to stick an Maximized Empowered (18x) Bull's Strength, Maximized Empowered (18x) Cat's Grace, etc etc, into one teensy item, whose restrictions I got to choose (see below, the last example, for details), which means I get a free item that gives me (4+1) * 1.5^18 = +7389 to all stats. Then a random lich pissed me off, so I threw an asteroid at him (jumped into space, grappled the sumbitch, and flung it at him, dealing hideous quantities of damage, even after he saved for half... a strength of 7400 gave me a bonus of 3695 to damage )

---

First, you ask your GM how long you have before the campaign starts to make your own magical equipment. He, assuming you're gonna be playing a spellcaster, gives you a number. I love it when they're generous. It stops to matter at a certain point, though. You'll see what I mean.
There comes a time in an adventurer's career that he has enough money to buy a ring that lets him use a Wish once per day, with a certain number of charges.
[9 (spell level) * 17 (caster level) * 1800 (command word activated) + 25,000 (XP cost)]
/ [5 (once per day) * 2 (50 total charges)] = 30,040 gp, which a starting level 9 character can afford easily.
So the instant you get the ring, you use it to get 15,000 gp, as one of the uses of Wish lets you do. On the second day, you do the same thing, getting another 15,000 gp. You do that for about two more days, and use your new 60,000 gp along with your money you have left over from being lvl 9 (about 36,000 gp to start off with) to buy a ring that lets you Wish twice per day, still 50 charges and all, which costs you 60,080 (you just make the "/ 5" into a "/ (5/2)", and that gets you double the original amount). So the next step is to go for a 3/day Wish. The cost is 30,040 * 3 = 90,120, which takes you about 3 days with your new 2/day ring. So now you have your 3/day wish, and you need a 4/day item... that takes you about 3 days. Then take your 4/day item and get one that doesn't have a limit on number of times per day, which costs about 138,950 gp. Bah, you can get that in a little more than two days.
Ok, now that you have a 50-charge ring of Wish, ya know what you're gonna do with it? You're gonna use 'em all up, laddy! 50 Wishes for 15,000 gp each gives you about 750,000 gp to play with. Use that to get a ring of Wishing with no restrictions (no charges, no times/day), which costs about 300,400 gp. w00t.
You have about 450,000 gp left over... a little more due to profit in between buying x/day rings of Wish. Use that to buy a second ring, one of use-activated Time Stop, which costs about 9 * 17 * 2000 = 306,000 gp... no biggie.
So now you have an infinite amount of time to give yourself 15,000 gp whenever you want. 15,000 gp times infinity is just about equal to an infinite amount of gold, give or take a few hundred quadrabajilliondy.
So a 9th level character with 13 days to kill gets everything he damn well feels like getting.

---
Building onto that:

You ever notice that segment in the DMG (3rd Edition) that lets you take off for various restrictions? How about making so many goddamn restrictions on the item you want to buy that the cost becomes next to nothing?
True story:
Me: "I know you want us to make 8th level characters, but can I play a 0-level commoner instead?"
DM: "Uh... sure, I guess."
Me: "Because I'm making this sacrifice, can I have the right to purchase my own custom-made magic items?"
DM: "Yeah, why not."
Me: "I win."
DM: "You what?"
Me: "I win. I just won. I beat DnD."
Basically, for those of you familiar with Precalculus...
the limit of the price of an item as the number of restrictions I can think of approaches infinity is 0. I can take off as much as 10% for anything I want... colored eyes, colored hair, number of hairs, height, weight, what I had for breakfast on that one day, that twitch I did in my sleep when I was a kid... as long as I have a history, I can make an infinite amount of restrictions. Any price * .9^x as x goes to infinity is 0, no matter the original price. So my 0-level commoner with the right to buy whatever the hell he wants gets a wittle ring that's use-activated Time Stop, and Wish, and whatever the hell else I want to throw in there. He instantly has infinite wealth, quite literally, and infinte power with the kind of shit he can buy with his infinte wealth.

---

#38273 14 2004-11-28T06:03:15Z Tsukatu
Two horsemen... I killed two. And their "horses" were just motorcycles, and their swords/sickles were dual-weilded M16s... I guess it's kind of a loose adaptation, but whatever. He fired 26 shots at me, hitting once, and I fired four shots at him, hitting all four times.
It seems you're confusing powergaming and perseverance. Getting 9,999 damage at 13th level is munchkinism, playing a game 12 times to see many different endings is perseverance; taking on the final boss without equipment and winning is munchkinism, being level 87 when you're supposed to be level 11 is perseverance.
For example, I have too many friends already who have breezed through FF7 simply because they devoted two or three months to staying in the very first map (at the rail station, leading to the mako reactor) and leveled up to insane levels before proceeding any further.
The book you quoted agrees with me too. It's not achievement through patience, but rather exploitations of ambiguous rules that leads to satisfying success. Well, in my true opinion, I don't think you can write a book about munchkinism. It's an individual skill that is unique to people and untranslatable to ink and paper. It's like talent as opposed to skill, y'know?

So I like the exploitation of ambiguous rules and unconventional use of underestimated methods to success aspects better than the achievements through patience, luck, and circumstance. In other words, I'm more interested in how you were able to dominate the Celerity 7 Vampire so easily instead of the fact that you did it.
I'm sure I've told you about the night one of our (worse) DMs got a little crazy on sugar and decided to host a 64th level campaign...
I made a wizard, and he let me dedicate the XP of 25 levels to creation of my own spells. Everyone else naturally went for fighting/rogue classes, thinking how awesome they were and how much havoc they could cause with their bare hands, while I went for the more studious and time-consuming path of the wizard. Those other poor sods just didn't want to mess with numbers. Anyway, even though I was by far the lowest level in the party (39th level, compared to 64th level characters), I could kick the everloving donkey shit out of the rest of the party members... at what they did best!
I could outsneak the rogue and had a higher Death Attack DC (assassin), had a higher initiative, and did more damage than he did when he applied sneak attack damage.
I could outrun the monk and do more damage unarmed, with a higher attack bonus and higher saves (by a factor of 14 or so... that is, my save bonuses were 14x his).
I had more HP than the fighter and did more damage than him, too, when he got every bonus he could think of and I was naked with my hands.
This is another clear example of munchkinism: everyone starts out with the same potential, but you rise to the top.
(Just because I want to gloat, my intelligence exceeded four digits, and the rest of my stats were upper 900's, all through epic spells, nothing more. It was all beautifully legal.)

Alright, I've decided to kind of pop my head in periodically, read the few latests posts, and comment if I have anything.
In this case, I do have something: a contrasting view of dwarves.
I might be alone, but I've always seen dwarves as the largest enemy to nature. Think about it this way...
Their mannerisms don't agree with nature. They're born in mountains (that's why they're so hardy, after all). Mountains produce dwarves. In those mines, they like to dig tunnels. Digging tunnels makes a race kind of buff and manly-like, which is what dwarves are. There's no particular advantage to height, so dwarves remained short (go Darwinism!). Being manly tends to build up testosterone, which contributes to more passionate anger and discrimination, in a mild sense. That is, they become short-tempered and impatient. When you think of a druid, you think of a patient, benevolent figure, right? What kind of dwarf will tolerate living in the forest? They're not patient enough, and they don't need their manliness and buffness to survive at all. Beyond that, dwarves like to mine things and dig tunnels and bang on pieces of metal with other pieces of metal. Where can you do any of that in a forest?
You're describing an elf, with all that forest business. If you put a human in a forest, you get an elf. If you put a human on a mountain, you get a dwarf. It's really that simple.
"Roughing it," eh? I call that a Wood Elf. Do you know how buff those guys are? (+2 Str, +2 Dex, -2 Con, -2 Int, -2 Cha, for those of you who play DnD) You don't need resilience and toughness to last in the forest, you just need to be able to kill things around you, while dwarves need to endure harsh climate and long work hours.

Do we have an official name for the snakepeople yet? From random descriptions I've seen above, they look like a yuan-ti... or if we want a simpler term, we have something extremely close to it in another system. In the glorious land that is Rokugan, we call those things Nagas. It's just easier to refer to them that way. Of course, in Rokugan, they're also about 3 times the size of a human and at least that many times as strong, but we can still call 'em what they look like.

Ookay, if you really get desperate, I'd suggest playing around with your registry editor.
Go to Start -> Run, and type in "regedit" and press enter. Ok, now lemme guess, the thing isn't giving you priveleges to access the registry editor, right? If that happens, go to Start -> Run again, and type in:
REG add HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v DisableRegistryTools /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
...and press enter.
Ok, then find the software thing in the registry, probably somewhere in HKCU\Software or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion or something, depending on how big of an impact this thing has on your system. No, Bricky, the rat-people comment wasn't addressing you or your previous statements.

I have some questions/theories for ya then:
1. Every dwarf I've seen focuses on the blacksmithing aspect. They're infatuated with mythril because it's so easy to work, which suggests further affinity to blacksmithing. Beyond that, why do the dwarves stay and mine? Why do they hang around those hostile environments? Market purposes? That's laughable. Dwarves like lots of thick metal stuff surrounding them, and their thick metal stuff is the coolest because they know how to make it. Dwarves live in the forge.
2. This was the cause of my abyss comment:
Quote: Bricky, 2004-12-02T03:05:32Z
They are the only ones who posses mines, because they and their allies (when I refer to allies, I mean armel and gnomes, because even though humans are on their side that is due only out of fear of crossing them) have made sure that any mines not run by dwarfs is destroyed, and that the miners and anyone with knowledge of minerals who isn't a dwarf is killed. Thus, they hold the only means of creating 95% of midevil weaponry.
Wait... wait, what!? You've gotta be kidding me. Do you realize how many wars this would cause? Surely leading dwarven officials are smarter than that, and gnome/halfling government officials don't want war, so they'll stay out of it. It's quite a task shutting down all of the other mining facilities and killing anyone who develops the idea of a pickaxe. In other words, your idea is absurd.
It's like... and this is about the appropriate power scale... Germany suddenly decides that it doesn't want America to manufacture anything. So it sends in all of its midgets with weapons they don't entirely know how to use, along with their French and Italian allies (midgets in the same predicament) and invade America, burning all of its department stores, warehouses, factories, etc, down to the ground, and kill anyone who understands the concept of "buy low, sell high." Naturally America, fearful of the wrath of the German midgets, decides not to retaliate, and lives subordinate to the awesome market that Germany becomes.
Does that sound reasonable to you? I worry for you if it does.
3. This goes along with #2, but it was getting long, so I'll put this as #3. Do you understand that when a weapon is made (for a war or whatever) that the weapon does not vanish into thin air when the need for it is gone? Dwarves may have a monopoly on iron (assuming they do, even though it's ridiculous), but they don't have a grip at all on the weapons market. Once that iron is sent out, weapons are made, and those are bought and sold like crazy. At the rate that dwarves are pumping out iron (they're the only ones who have it, and I'm assuming they want to stay financially balanced), within a few decades, the need for iron will be pretty much gone. There used to be high demand, but now that the rest of the civilizations have massive supplies, no one needs metal from the dwarves anymore, because they already have it, and their own markets are doing the work distributing it in various forms. Dwarves are suddenly out of a job.
Speaking of weapons markets, where do the dwarves expect to get their weapons? You said they're not smiths, so they'd have to import. Who in their right mind would not demand higher iron availability when exporting weapons to the dwarves? This kills the hideous economic superiority that the dwarves have, so they're not on top anymore. Have you also considered that smiths can repair/improve weapons that already exist? Sure, all they have to do is smelt them down and remake them, usually improving their quality. Who needs iron anymore, seriously?
4. This is just some naivete:
Quote: Bricky, 2004-12-02T03:05:32Z
And the modernized technology (rifles, cannons) were invented by gnomish inventors, who gave the secrets of making them to the dwarves as a way of gaining an eternal "protected" status and because they had not enough access to the resources needed to produce them.
What kind of world have you been living in? A country never shares its secrets with another country. Even if gnomes didn't have the resources to make their coolness, it'd be a simple matter of purchasing iron like they normally do or call in most of their weapons (gnomes will find that turning their dagger into a plasma cannon is quite worth it), telling the dwarves that they just want to make shortswords and armor, so that they can defend themselves against the [insert race here]. The dwarves sell it, and gnomes use it to make an legion of hovertanks. Then they go behind the dwarves backs...
Gnomes: "Hey, you guys..."
Humans, Elves, Halflings: "Yeah, what?"
Gnomes: "You like iron?"
Humans, Elves, Halflings: "Yeah."
Gnomes: "You want free iron?"
Humans, Elves, Halflings: "Of course."
Gnomes: "OK, let's go kill some dwarves. They can't build or use weapons, and we have cool weapons that we know how to use. They don't have any allies. They also have it coming, with their selfish need to be on top economically. Like stealing a sack of $100's from a dead baby..."
Humans, Elves, Halflings: "Alrighty."
And then all the races gang up and eat the dwarves, and there's iron for everybody, especially the gnomes, who can then use it for their own plots... yadda yadda.
5. Fun with quotes:
Quote: Brickie, 2004-12-02T03:05:32Z
Dwarves are as good as anyone with those weapons
Quote: Brickie, 2004-12-02T03:05:32Z
dwarves are not nimble enough to use [those weapons] effectively
6.This I found interesting:
Quote: Brick-san, 2004-12-02T03:05:32Z
other races lost the knowledge of how to gather minerals via mines and thus they could not produce their own metal even if the dwarves couldn't catch them
Mining is an extremely easy concept. Let's take the world you've made right now, and I'll show you how you have chaos once time moves for about six and a half minutes.
A human farmer is out in his fields with a hoe, digging up some roots, when he comes across a big rock. He needs the rock out of the way so he can grow crops. So he digs around the rock, maybe even chips off small edges of the rock, and pulls the sucker out. Beneath the rock he finds some naturally formed crystals. He thinks they look pretty. Getting out of the hole, he sees that the underside of the rock is covered in these things, since they came from the rock. So he bangs on the rock in such a fashion as to loosen the crystals from their positions. He goes to town and sells the pretty looking things so that they can be made into jewelry and such. Then he goes back to his farm and digs up his fields, finding more naturally-made gems, mostly imbedded into rock.
This farmer has just discovered mining. I'm willing to bet that a good chunk of each population (I'll wager up to 70%) will all discover mining by themselves, if the concept isn't related to them.
Since when do dwarves "catch" people mining? When a dwarf is visiting a human settlement and he gets nosy, I'd tell him to get the hell out. I have a right to, after all, and I can say that he is not to go beyond a certain point (a few miles in from the borders... the human mines being at the center) because that area is owned by the human governments, and any attempt to enter will be constituted as an act of war. How're they gonna bypass that, dwarven ninjas? Stilt-wearing dwarven spies? No human will spy for them, they'll hate the dwarves for being that bloody arrogant. It's not like any normal human will be able to see human mines anyway, since it's a covert government project.

If humans have the capability of inventing bows, then humans will invent bows whether the elves want them to or not.

Since when do elves care about getting back at dwarves? Dwarves aren't hurting the environment much at all, they're just digging and sifting. Ain't nothing wrong with digging and sifting. Luckily, elves have this little "you touch my tree, I will flay you, your friends, your relatives, and your friends' relatives, and dance around with your heads before defacating on your ancestors' graves" policy, and that's the family-friendly version.
Elves are haughty, they don't care. They also sure as hell don't need allies.

Centrifugal force (I'm assuming you're referring to that) does not exist. It does not exist in any form of anything remotely resembling the distant cousin of any frame of reference. Doesn't exist, didn't ever exist, never will exist. It's just people misnaming Centripetal force, thinking it is directed away from the center.
Centripetal force is not any extension of gravity. Centripetal force is a force in the same way that pulling on a yo-yo is a force. In fact, that's pretty much exactly what it is, except that the yo-yo is whirling around your hand.
Wow, I've accidentally run across one of the most comprehensible examples for it. That's a first.
When you don't have a string, like when a car is making a wide, circular turn, or when a ninja with a horrendously fast metabolism runs into a vertical U-turn, inertia becomes involved... but if there's something physical roping the center of the circle to the object twirling, inertia isn't really relevant.

#1564 1 2004-12-03T05:24:43Z Tsukatu
Character Bio:

Name: Sargvaas
Race: Human
Age: 27
Region: Haven't decided yet
Profession: Berserker/Mercenary
Bio:
Sargvaas grew up on the streets of [metropolitan human city I haven't decided upon yet] as an orphan. He was raised by a group of street thugs, whom he had witnessed steal and murder for the first six years of his life. When his gang was finally caught by city officials, he managed to hide away, and wasn't caught. From then on, he had to resort to taking action himself in order to get food and such. As a boy, he slept high up on a rooftop of a wealthy family's house, who never found out about it. He would rise early in the morning and head straight into the slums of the city, where he eventually founded a small gang of orphans. Because of their young age and their nature, he had to frequently discipline his gang, and so became a quite capable fighter. Soon, other neighborhood boys got the same idea, and by age 13, he was looking at gang warfare across the city. He had moved into an abandoned block of houses in the slums, and his gang used this as a sort of base of operations. At this point in his life, he still did not have a name; everyone just referred to him as "the boss."
Children yet so young did not have the stomach for fighting with weapons, so the main form of fighting was with one's own fists. Sargvaas enjoyed fighting, he loved it. His gang made a name for itself as the most militant gang in his part of town. During a confrontation with another gang, he would charge ahead of his gang (and became pretty athletic) and immediately, at the start of the fight, be within striking range of as many enemies as could fit, and somehow last through the initial part of the fight and continue to take down the opposition with incredible alacrity. His favorite battle tactic has always been, and will most likely always be, fear.
Back at home, he would spend his time lifting crude weights. He believed that if he were to be the strongest, the gods would favor him and pay special attention to him, especially his patron deity, the god of strength and luck, with a heavy lean toward recklessness in combat. So far, his faith has not let him down, and he does seem to be favored by his god, as he escapes unscathed out of impossible situations, in which he places himself, routinely. Over the years, he has also become by far the strongest of the gang leaders physically due to his habit of lifting weights when he thinks, eats, is nervous, etc.
When he turned 16, things took a nasty turn for his gang. A new member joined his ranks, and quickly displaces him as gang leader. When he challenged the newcomer for the top position, he was deceived and run out of town. He wandered alone for a month or so, barely finding enough food to survive, usually from passing merchants and messengers (whom he ambushed, which sometimes got him in a bit of trouble). While wandering particularly far from civilization one evening, he found himself surrounded by lizardmen (near the desert... try and tell me a snake is more adapted for the desert than a lizard), who knocked him out and took him home out of curiosity. It turns out that he was the first human they had seen, and so they began playing with him. When they realized he could work, they offered to include him in their tribe. He was very much like them, not surprisingly, and enjoyed their company. He was slowly taught their language, and in return he attempted to teach them his. The result was his fluency in their language (he was surrounded by them, and that was the only language he could speak with them in), and their loose understanding of a heavy street dialect of his language. He was also taught to read and write their language, and he regretted never having picked up a book (to read, anyway; he had probably bashed in some skulls with dictionaries) and never learning to read.
When he was 19, his tribe met another lizard tribe, and war broke out. He fit right in, fighting exceptionally for a human, yet on par with a lizardman. After a few more wars, involving usage of weapons, blood, and death, he became a more adept fighter than even the lizardmen in his tribe, rivaling their chieftan. After seeing him in combat, the lizardmen decided to give him an appropriate name: Sargvaas, meaning "the bloody-handed" in their tongue (they had previously referred to him as "Human," as in, "hey Human, pass the goat").
One fateful day, their tribe moved too close to a town and began receiving harassment from city guards and mercenaries... so they decided to do what any rational tribe would do: they sacked and burned the town. Sargvaas noticed that he felt no tie to humans, since they had shown him no compassion or honesty, while he felt right at home with his lizardman tribe. They gained plenty of loot from the town, and Sargvaas became interested in human culture again. The lizardmen had made an attempt to speak in his human tongue to keep his fluency in it, and it paid off during their assault on the town, causing confusion and panic among the city guard.
The tribe was also very interested in humans, and so they began preying on small villages and hamlets. In doing this, Sargvaas obtained a few suits of armor of exceptional quality (from captains of the city guard, mainly, which only fit him in his tribe) and human weapons. He realized that he was actually far better using human weapons, since he had been using unweildly (for him) lizardman weapons, and his massive strength and speed (do you know how hard it is to swing a greatclub that's a size category too large for you about as fast as a drawn katana? that's how this guy learned) made him an awesome force to reckon with in melee combat.
At about the age of 24, his tribe had migrated to his home city, and Sargvaas became consumed with a need for revenge. He convinced his tribe to make a full-scale attack on his home city, in his old slums district. He went in by himself to a different part of town and bought (with spoils from other towns) several large cloaks, which he gave to his tribe. His tribe, however, was having doubts, and so those who believed in him separated from those who didn't want the attack (Sargvaas' invading force included 7 of the fiercest warriors of his tribe and their chieftan, the rest stayed back).
Sargvaas and his crew walked deep into the heart of his old slum district during the night, all wearing heavy cloaks that concealed their appearances. He quickly found his old base of operations and entered silently. Taking his old gang (whom he had forsaken) and their new boss (the same one that displaced Sargvaas) by surprised, it was an incredibly easy victory, and all that was his ex-gang lay in bloody chunks on the ground. He had gotten personal revenge against the gang leader, by the way, and it was a very short fight: he swung three times, missing, shattering the leader's weapon, and finally cutting him in half across his torso, the whole fight lasting less than four seconds. However, when another gang crashed the party, as their idea of a secret midnight attack, the lizardmen got carried away and began killing any human they saw. Sargvaas went with them, and they managed to bring down a few gangs, some of them neither entirely involved nor directly hostile to them. The city guard finally rushed in, and after a long fight involving the deaths of countless gangmembers and city officials (kill:death ratio was about 26:1 for Sargvaas and his buddies... they caused quite some havoc), the lizardmen lay dead, and Sargvaas returned to hiding.
He escaped the city and moved to far-away lands, where he built up a reputation as a hired mercenary. Within a month of moving away, he received news that his old town had fallen to lizardmen... apparently the more peaceful members of his original tribe saw that the city became extremely vulnerable after Sargvaas' suicidal assault, and they gathered allies and took the city by storm. Newspapers explained that they came in two waves: one expert group to serve as a first wave, and then the second wave, ten times the size, came in for a crushing victory over the city. Lizardmen then flooded into the city and settled there, becoming the first major city of lizardmen in history, its population soaring to rival the old human population. In a way, it triggered a new cultural revolution for the lizardmen. Only few papers mentioned a rumor of a human leading their first charge, and these rumors quickly disappeared and were deemed irrelevant, with suggestions that the human had died during the attack.
For three years, Sargvaas has lived as a mercenary. He has been a town guard, a member of the militia, and an extremely reliable messenger, but the biggest demand for him has been in the position of bodyguard. His strength and fighting instinct in conjunction with his strong faith family have made him a loyal and fierce warrior, and his fighting style has given him the title of "berserker" by those who have seen him fight. If not for his attempts to keep his profile low, Sargvaas would become a legend in his region, especially given the stories his men-at-arms in his guard and militia days are more than willing to retell.
Sargvaas is currently unemployed, but is hoping to find a new employer in the town in which the campaign will start.
His preferred attire is a very finely crafted set of full-plate, which he got custom-fitted as a favor by the mayor of one particular town for outstanding work as a mercenary, painted a deep red, with black and gold etchings, which would be very recognizable if not for the very heavy cloak he wears to conceal his entire body. He keeps his hood up most of the time and his cloak open only enough to barely see his deep red plate, when looking at the right angle. His brooch was another gift from one of his female employers, and is a design of two lizards biting each others' tails. On his back, he carries his preffered weapon (a greatsword, more below), a crude maul (from his tribal days, more of a good luck charm... that works, apparently), and four javelins. Inside his cloak, on his belt, he has a pair of bastard swords, and a shattered longsword without a sheath, dangling from a chain (the property of the gang leader who displaced him, also a good luck charm).
His preffered weapon is a finely crafted serrated greatsword with a crimson blade, matching his armor, which he ordered to be crafted by the most reputable blacksmith in the country. The hilt is pretty much featureless and is specially designed for his massive grip. The sword is built especially for him... a person of his phenomenal strength and approximate height.
As for his physical appearance, he has dark brown eyes, and the same color hair that he keeps a few inches long to stay out of the way. He otherwise doesn't maintain his hair. He has a crooked nose and a slightly displaced jaw from fights in his earlier days. Surprisingly, he has no scars or deformations on his face aside from the broken nose and unnoticable jaw displacement. Covering his face is stubble he maintains at a very short length.Sargvaas stands six and a half feet tall, but tends to slouch and lumber, putting him at a usual 5'11".
Sargvaas prefers to charge almost blindly into battle, putting himself specifically in the most dangerous position available, from which he can reach the most enemies.
When he enters combat, he isn't irrationally angry, but is instead more like a tactician. He commonly barks out orders (or "suggestions," as he calls them after the battle if he can't pull rank on his comrades), which change over to the lizard language when he becomes very involved. Sargvaas otherwise wishes to defer attention from his association with lizardmen.

Edit:
Awwrighty, after reading the blurb on humans...
Sargvaas escaped his old city by boat just barely, and spent a few years wandering back to his home to exact his revenge. So subtract the total time he spent with lizardmen by one or two years. His hometown was Armonia, whether it be populated mostly by humans or not. He wandered back through the western pass after landing in Aeken when he escaped, and was captured by lizardmen near Shilin. They migrated slowly in almost a beeline toward Armonia, sacking settlements along the way that are too small to be put on a political map. After helping to cripple Armonia, he took a boat down to Lorn, and has been wandering between Fedon, Markon, and Lorn, looking for work. Much of his more military-based work was done near Lorn and Markon, keeping the Armell in check. After fighting other lizardmen in the past, up north, Sargvaas finds that his greatsword goes through Armell and their armor like a hot knife through butter. It's actually satisfying and easy to cut one in half, including the armor (for him, anyway). Various militant Armell groups, especially bandits, have met their end in Lorn under Sargvaas' blade, and the Armell population has decreased dramatically with his coming (mostly fleeing in fear for the Crimson Vanguard, or whatever they want to call him).

Edit Edit:
One other thing I forgot to slip in that I was planning. Another explanation behind his strength was... well... how would you expect little kids to get food? Stealing will get you caught and put in the slammer, and he didn't want to have to resort to beating up a city official or anything. So instead, just for profit, Sargvaas and his gang started selling drugs, usually stuff they stole from other, older gangs or other gangs. But they never sold anything like steroids. Until Sargvaas saw the negative effects of that stuff, he used the steroids himself. He fought off his addiction successfully after living with the tribe for so long. Lack of availability kinda weans you off that stuff.

I'm assuming you don't have eyes in the back of your head. No amount of skill can help you avoid an arrow shooting at you behind your back.
Elves that travel around aren't that powerful, and elves that live quiet live in cities (even elven cities) are just as powerful, if not slightly less powerful, than humans. However, because of their long lifespan, those chosen to guard the elven kingdom are trained far more thoroughly than any other standing army. The elven army is a damn fearsome thing. If only they didn't focus on defense....
But anyway, any guards you find are going to have state-of-the-art armor and weapons are are going to be able to take, individually, two or three, or even four human footsoldiers at one time, assuming the humans get the jump on them and that they're not allowed to use their bows. You simply don't mess with elves.

So if you want to be a legend, go with 1:1 odds against elves, and corner them somewhere and turn it into a slaughter. You can still say that you escaped captivity by a dozen elven forest guards, and then successfully avoided further stupidity all the way to Cordo. Going through the elven forest without permission is a crazy idea that only the pro's should attempt... and you did it! Congrats, you're a legend!

As for equipment, go for plate armor, full-body (though not full plate, there is a difference), finely crafted swords, a high quality war-trained steed with chain barding, and a lance or something, because you might as well.

Sargvaas, meanwhile, is working frantically to appoint generals, organize the tribes, draft constitutions, draft battle plans, especially defense plans, and figuring out which races are where in relation to him. He's never seen a map before... not that he could read a human one, anyway, and lizardmen don't have maps... Oh joy, another item to add to the list: training and sending out scouts, organizing an army based on ability and leadership capabilities, and then training some diplomats.

By the end of the day (which I know we haven't gotten to yet), Sargvaas had appointed four generals and twenty seargants, organizing them under the generals (two to defend, one from each side (east and west), and two to prepare offensives (one to each side)), and then let the seargants appoint subordinates themselves, who appointed their own subordinates... well, that took a lot of work out of his hands, provided he had chosen people who were competent enough to pick subordinates competent enough to pick subordinates who were competent enough...

Alright, he had it figured out... each general has 5 seargants. The defensive seargants will focus on one method of defense and spread themselves by lieutenants across their respective border. They'd have to invent various methods of defending provinces, and Sargvaas left that to the generals and seargants. The other 10 seargants under the two offensive generals would specialize based on necessity. Two seargants of each general would focus on fire-based destruction, targetting the forests that flank the lizardmen territories. Sargvaas figured it was better to force a home-field advantage rather than fight the elves where they're used to fighting. Yes, better to burn it all down. Two lieutenants of one seargant under each general, preferrably the seargant more focused on light-armored hit-and-run tactics, would focus on information gathering. The rest of the divisions were to be decided upon by the generals and seargants themselves, based on ability. Each general was told to pick a versatile group of seargants, and the seargants were told the same about lieutenants.

He had sent orders to any craftsmen, whatever their craft, to start making things out of bone. Light bone armor would aid the light infantry, and bone walls were easy to make quickly, were intimidating (Sargvaas' favorite battle tactic was inciting fear, after all), and provided the minimal protection they so direly needed. Lastly, a fortress of bone was to be made in Arein, which was to become the capital. Sargvaas had plans to leave for Arein the following morning. He would use the time it took to get there to draft a constitution and to plan more thoroughly his plans for dominion.

The tribe Sargvaas was a member of before the takeover of Armonia had inherited the task of teaching some key officials the human tongue, who would then (hopefully) pass it on to preferred diplomats, who would be sent out to discuss matters with the elves and the armell.

"Organizing a nation sure is hard work," thought Sargvaas before he passed out from exhaustion that night.

Edit: Completely forgot about defense!

The general defense plans were to be the establishment of forts scattered in the two frontiers, each complete with networks of hidden tunnels that made travelling between them easy and reliable when under seige. That is, unless the an invading army somehow got wind of the underground passages between forts and managed to destroy the tunnels that were a little less than forty feet below the ground, a fort could survive a siege almost indefinitely. Opposing armies could travel along the same paths, one above-ground, moving slowly and facing the fury of sandstorms, dry heat, and silky sand in which their wagons and feet would sink, while the lizardman army could move with ease through the tunnels forty feet below.

Forts coming close to the main lizardman cities would be obvious and intimidating, while forts further out would be disguised as hills of sand. When an army passed over or around them, the lizardmen would jump out and, with the help of nearby dune-forts, surround and overwhelm the opposition.

Sargvaas figured he'd leave any ideas of subtely lowering numbers of an army by pulling them down underneath the sands to the generals and seargants.

Two of Szazgul's escorts were walking to their rooms (which the mayor gave to them at no charge; go diplomats!) from the local tavern in disappointment from not finding the same kinds of drinks they scavenged from human cities in the desert. They were discussing lifestyles and choices of scenery of the Armell, pointing out house structure and organization. Instantly, both of them caught a whiff of blood in the air. Following the scent, they came to a figure huddled against a door or a building they could not identify. They had already passed by two homeless men, not knowing what they were, and so they became curious when they came upon a third. The two noticed that he was sleeping, and so they decided to sneak up to it and see what it looked like.
The smell of blood was thick, alright. The thing had been injured recently. Whatever it was, it was pretty damn tired, because it didn't awake when one of them turned him over to see his face. Both of them almost jumped in surprise.
"Isn't this..."
"I think it is."
"Wow. Who would've thought he'd fall into our laps?"
"Yeah, crazy stuff. We need to make sure though. Here, he seems pretty tired. I'll take him to my room, you get Szazgul. We need to be sure."
"Alright."
One of the escorts took off running toward the center of the town, and the other moved to gently pick up the human.
---
Szazgul nodded. "That's him alright. I can't believe it. We'll take an emergency trip back or something. I'll make something up."
---
Needless to say, when Eversio finally woke up, he felt quite rested. However, it was dark where he was, and it smelled kind of bad. His entire body was cramped, and when he tried to stretch, he found himself bound very tightly by ropes. In fact, his whole body was covered in rope, tied very securely, with his feet tied to his hands behind him back. He tried to shout out, and discovered that he was gagged. So he tried one final attempt at getting free: he started thrashing around wildly. After a few seconds of thrashing, he heard scraping coming from the lid of whatever he was in, and then a latch opening. Whoever put him in this confounded box was going to pay. As the lid latch was opened, he prepared the most sickeningly pissed glare he could muster. His attitude, however, changed completely when the face that showed was that or a huge green monster, with piercing yellow eyes and a draconian snout, lined with pointy teeth. It looked at him, amused, and then hissed something to another out of Eversio's line of sight. There was a reply, and the thing in front of him chuckled. Keeping the lid open with one hand, it pulled from beside it Eversio's razor chain, and asked something to him in a mocking tone, gesturing to the chain. After staring into Eversio's horrified eyes for a few more moments, it closed the lid again, and the box latched closed.
---
The next time the lid was opened, there was a different face waiting for him. It was still monstrous, like the previous one, but it wasn't the same creature. It quietly removed the gag, and spoke to him eloquently in a language he understood.
"Hello, Eversio. In case you were a bit confused, my superior would like to have a word with you. I believe you'll find his deal to be quite acceptable in your favor."

Mojo, you can reply to it if you want. If not, he closes the lid and you're locked in again, with stuff put on top of your box.

Or, y'know, you should step into a physics classroom or pick up a textbook. I've had plenty of problems for homework or on tests or whatever that involved a car going around a corner, some random particle making a u-turn, a rollercoaster going on a loop-de-loop, etc, and we went over them in class using the rules for centripetal (not fugal, fugal doesn't exist and is used by the uneducated) forces. Those situations are simply within the definition of centripetal forces.
Momentum has precisely nothing to do with it. I'm serious, nothing. Momentum is relevant when you have, say, object A of mass M1 that hits object B of mass M2, and you need to know how fast A and B go after their collision based on M1 and M2, as well as initial velocities of A and B. Collisions, basically, because I know you're staring at the screen in wonderment. That or if you have a dog on a boat, and the dog walks to one side of the boat and the boat moves opposite the dog in the water. Those are all good examples.

It's centripetal force, and pretty much nothing else.

Dusk came slowly. At about the peak of his boredom, Eversio noticed the spiny walls of some form of fort in the distance.
"Are we close?" he asked the driver loudly. "How soon will we be in your lands?"
The driver looked back and smiled long enough for Eversio to grow suspicious. "We already here." With that, the driver pointed behind Eversio.
Barely managing to turn around in his restraints, Eversio was shocked to see so many camouflaged forts that he thought were sand dunes. They speckled the landscape as far as he could see. The nearest one had a few lizardman warriors, mostly fulfilling Eversio's stereotypical view of lizardman: loincloth-clad savages with spears. Well, they had glaives, which was a start, but their appearance didn't help. Among the nearest was a small group of humans bound in chains, all digging away at the side of a bunker wall. Some watched Eversio's chariot, recalling better times, but they were quickly reminded of their duties by sharp whacks on their heads from an overseer.
The chariot slowed down as it came nearer to the plainly visible fort, and came to a halt just inside its walls. In the fort, he was lifted again by some random lizardman and placed into another chariot in far better repair and decor. In the chariot was a more serious and older driver and another lizardman waiting for Eversio right behind the driver. Eversio was placed next to the second lizardman, who quickly filled Eversio in on where he was in almost unaccented human speech.
"Hello, Eversio. We've been waiting for you for some time now. This is one of our smaller forts a few miles away from Arein. Your last driver is still needed to deliver equipment and provisions from here to Mel, and various forts along the way, so you won't be seeing much more of him. We should arrive at Arein before dawn."
Part of what the thing said surprised him. If this well-defended, heavy fortification was a "small" fort, what did a large one look like? Oh well, they were lizardmen, and were probably preparing as they were used to against insane, combat-crazy warmongers... other lizardmen.
"You look tired. Sleep. Everything will be explained to you in Arein."

You can feel free to talk to him, or you can sleep, I don't really care. Things will pick up for you in Arein, I swear. Meanwhile, you can still choose to make a good impression on this dude, whoever he is.

On an entirely different note, why is my eye bleeding? This can't be good...

As their caravan bumped along on the forest road and the knight and dwarf questioned the prospector, a messenger on a horse ran up to them rather quickly. The driver stopped, and Detario and Sir Relnor got out to see what the problem was. Immediately after they had gotten out, the messenger halted his horse from its hasty pace in front of them. The messenger was a rather terrified dwarf, and he seemed quite anxious and nervous.
"Th-there's a c-call to arms! M-M-Morid is under attack!"
He looked over at Detario.
"Are you Detario Auhngrym? Y-your commanding officer orders you to get th-there as fast as p-possible. I was sent to ask assistance f-from the Armell. Hurry!"
With that the messenger raced off toward Fellos.

A day earlier, somewhere outside Morid:
"Yes, general, my theory is that they have gone so long without need for defense that they have nothing more than an inexperienced police force to protect them. We have seen the rest of their army toward the outskirts of their territories. They don't seem to be prepared for a naval assault, and they certainly aren't expecting anyone to pull this kind of stunt."
"Excellent," replied the general. "I want this done as quickly as possible. I will be needed back on the eastern front after this." (Time to play Guess the General )
"Yes, general."
The sargeant left the tent briskly, crouching beneath the low tent flap and almost knocking the whole thing over with his tail as he went. He made his way briskly to the rest of the detachment, who were busy eating and entertaining themselves. All focus went to the sargeant when they saw him.
"Settle in early. We attack before morning." He turned on his heel and left, to the cheering of the soldiers.
They were pretty optimistic about their planned raid, and they had reason to be. All of them were at least of lieutenant status, and they were among the best of the best in their tribes before settling into cities. Sargvaas wanted their first official raid to give their enemies the impression that they were invincible, and so "The Untouchables" were chosen for this attack - the ones who, in years of fighting in the front lines, had an uncanny ability to avoid being hit. This wasn't a sacking of a city as much as a robbery, anyway. It also served as a diversion to a slightly larger attack that would only be carried out when the dwarves were heavily occupied with the Morid fiasco.

I'll begin describing the scene and how they attack (with accordance to the purpose of the attack), since it's pretty unconventional, when you guys get there.

Eversio awoke to find himself unbound, in more elegant clothing, lying on a bed in what appeared to be a castle. The room was decorated for a woman, but much of the decoration was torn and stained with blood, which matched nicely with the blood-stained and scratched walls. His broadknife was on the dresser next to him, sticking up, with the tip of its blade stabbed into the wood. As he was adjusting to the light, what was apparently a guard left the room. By the time Eversio had risen from the bed and grabbed his broadknife, the same stern lizardman that sat with him on the ride over entered the room, flanked by guards.
"Sargvaas wishes to speak with you in two hours. We'll come get you. In the meantime, make yourself at home."
The lizardman and the guards left quickly, leaving Eversio confused and disoriented.
