From the northwest side, the side from which Relnor, Imir, and Detario approached, Morid seemed perfectly fine. More wagons and such joined them on the road to Morid, all for the same purpose, and so they looked like a hearty dwarven detachment. They were confused; no smoke was in sight, no bodies were strewn around the walls, and there were no established attempts to get over the walls. Once they approached, however, they heard a cry from the wall, yelling something about reinforcements. The wagons rushed down the road through the portcullis, which was wide open...
Morid's not a huge city, so I'm guessing this will work somewhat.
As they all rushed in through the gates and got out of their wagons, a small batallion of dwarves rushed to meet them. Ahead of them was a higher-ranking member of the city police.
"Good, we have reinforcements. The bastards made their way to the far end, toward the mines," he pointed at the end opposite the entry gate. "They're huge, unlike anything we've ever faced before. We're just the police force, there's not much we've been able to do to stop them. The army's on their way. For now, we need to keep ourselves alive and hold them off until the army comes. They don't seem to attack us if we're out of their way."
"How did they get in?" barked Relnor.
"They used humans! They said they were a merchant caravan from Kurzano, and when we opened the gate, they rolled in and took over the portcullis from the inside. We've already abandoned the walls, because we can't defend them from the inside... not against them!"
Sure enough, the way to the other end of the city was paved in blood. Dozens of pieces of dwarf were strewn messily through the streets. Whoever attacked either had dwarven support or was hard to kill.
Running through the streets toward the growing noise, the party eventually caught sight of a line of enourmous and fearsome humanoids clad entirely in bone armor. From the looks of them, and the direction of their attack, it might well be an army from Kurzano attacking them. Maybe the humans decided that they wanted metal at a cheaper cost?
The line was virtually unopposed; it looked like the bulk of the police force's defensive force met their makers, because in front of the line was a naturally-formed wall of armored dwarven chunks ™. It wasn't clear what was going on behind them.
It was then that the party realized that most of the noise was simply the screaming of panicked commoners as they frantically grabbed their belongings and flooded the streets, looking to flee.
As their group advanced (the "reinforcements") and slowed down before the untouched (it was untouched for the most part... one or two had a javelin sticking out of his arm or leg) line of enemy soldiers, a larger figure made his way toward them, pushing past the line. Relnor/Imir/Detario's group stopped forty or so feet before the line, organizing themselves in the most secure offensive formation they could think of. The larger figure stopped five feet ahead of his line.
It was a lizardman. He had the same bone armor that his soldiers had, but his was far thicker and of better quality. He wore lots of red silk underneath and around his armor, as well as a thick red cloak. On his back were two very large claymores. He was easily recognized as a lizardman because he wasn't wearing a helmet. He addressed their group, who were outnumbered horribly by the line of soldiers.
"Looks like Morid sent for reinforcements. I'm afraid you missed the action. We were just leaving."
Behind him, there was a tremendous explosion, and part of the wall behind them collapsed. Then another, which left the wall hanging barely, and a third and fourth that flattened that area of the wall completely.
"You can waste your lives if you so choose. Some of us are getting hungry, so it might even be requested." He gave a knowing look at one of the larger soldiers in the front lines, who let out a nasty bellow. A few others patted his shoulders.
"We will leave long before further reinforcements show, so don't try anything too heroic." With that, he spun on his heel and went back through his 5-man thick line to the back of the city.
The opposing sides stared at each other awkwardly.
There was tremendous commotion going on behind the line, and soon it was apparent what the lizards were after: massive chunks of unrefined iron ore were moved very efficiently through the hole in the wall.
The dwarven police official in their group threw down his helmet in anger and cursed loudly.
"There isn't much we can do... at least we have our lives, gentlemen."
Slowly, the line of lizardmen receded through the hole, and as the dwarves chased them out, they saw in the horizon that the ocean in the not-so-far distance was covered in ships and vessels of all sizes.

Hey Brickman, what do you get when you take every single aspect of the old human cities' navy (that lizards have captured) and parade them down to the dwarven coast to steal as much iron as they can? Not much iron, but I can tell you now that it's far more than you think, because Morid's not the only source.

The last volley of shots was fired futily (sp?) at the receding lizardman army, who were by now rolling through the mountain pass in various vehicles, including two dwarven buildings that were literally uprooted and given wheels.
A dwarven officer ran to their group, looking rather pale, and held out a note to the police official.
"This just came. Forr is under attack. They request assistance."
The official just gave him a blank look. Then he turned toward Relnor/Detario/Imir.
"I'm needed here to clean up and salvage our losses. I'm assuming you guys are the leaders of this band," he gestured to the 40 or so dwarves behind them that came with them to Morid, answering the call to arms. "Go down to Forr and see if things there look any more hopeful."

You did have dwarven support when you rushed over to Morid. That's the key word though, rushed. The dwarven army hasn't been used in ages, because everyone is too afraid to cross them thanks to your own little monopoly idea. I was just using that against you. There's no way the dwarven army can organize and move away from dwarven borders that quickly. The lizardmen, after reaching the shore, camped for the night, then put themselves in wagons (that they had brought on their boats, probably), and had some human slaves dress up like merchants and request to enter Morid. Dwarves trade with people, yes? Merchants sell things to dwarves, right? This is pretty routine, so the dwarves let them in. Once the first wagon is in, a bunch of lizardmen hop out and as quickly as they can take over the gate and pull it wide open for the rest of their army to come. From that point, the rest of the attack force stormed into the now opened gates, sprinted their way to the end with mines and such, and immediately, at most 20 minutes into the attack, they had their army protecting that section of Morid while people behind them immediately began digging some tunnels to undermine the wall. Another large chunk of them went to start stealing the iron ore and putting it into a transportable form.
Eli, the reason people didn't attack is because they're not all suicidal. If you were among about 40 dwarves, all with axes and armor and such, and you were facing 80 lizardmen, all fully-decked out, with dead dwarves that are just as armored and skilled as you lying at their feet, while they are untouched, I think it's pretty realistic to say that you wouldn't charge that line. If you wanted to go and attack the sargeant (that's who it was), all he had to do was step back five feet while you ran the 35 feet to him and let his soldiers liquify you, or just whip out his claymores and do it himself. A lizardman is stronger and more skilled than you, especially these guys (who were chosen specifically because of their skill), and there are more of them. It's like 40 children charging 80 navy seals... you can try, but you will fail, and there probably won't be many casualties. May I remind you that the dwarven support you had was mainly comprised of police who aren't used to fighting a)skilled b)lizardmen c)invaders?
You guys spent the day getting to Morid. News came to you long after Morid was attacked, which was definitely after the lizards began undermining and robbing. By the time you got there, the lizards had had all day to organize themselves... and you guys just rushed over! ("Rushing" is something the army can't do as fast as "free agents" like you guys)
The idea behind the attack was to get in, get the iron, and get out as quickly as friggin possible. There is no way the lizards could take the approaching dwarven army, and there's no way they can sack and take over dwarven cities.
The attack was more of a chicken-wimp hit-and-run attack on a small city on the outskirts of dwarven territory when they least expected it. It's nothing more.

Morid was the only city attacked so far, and now Forr is suffering the same thing, but under far better leadership (Guess the General). Notice anything similar between Morid and Forr? They're both small cities on the outskirts of dwarven territory that have little reason to be guarded.

Your battle scene, Brickman, assumes that the lizardmen wanted a full-on takeover of the city and made no attempt to do it discreetly. It didn't coincide at all with the purpose of attacking Morid.
Pigeons are fast, but armies are not. Kurzano probably got the message and started sending over boats, and I bet you the human navy will chase the lizardman army back to Arein, sinking half of their ships in the process, but it's not possible for them to move all the way up through that land to catch the lizardmen as they walked through the gate.
You got the message while lizardmen were finishing up their undermining work. You sent the pigeon, and its trip to Kurzano took just about as much time as you took to get to Morid (assuming that a pigeon could move three times as fast as your charging horse, which is pretty damn fast for a pigeon). Kurzano heard word just about the same time as you guys because of Morid's own messengers, so I'm not sure what the poing of the pigeon was anyway. Assuming Kurzano could move as quickly as you guys (which they can't nearly), they'd reach Morid just as the lizardmen were leaving anyway.

To sum it up:
Lizardmen are not invincible, and the point of the attack was to move as quickly as possible to get iron and high-tail it out of there.
They fled long before reinforcements that weren't rushed (like you guys) could get there.
Morid is perfectly fine. It just has some minor repairs to do on a wall, and there are only a few dozen dwarven casualties, only a handful of them civilians. Nothing else was burned or destroyed, just some ore was stolen. That's all. No takeover, no seige, just wussy larceny.
Forr is suffering the same thing, an unexpected hit-and-run attack that does nothing but kill a handful of dwarves who get in the way, a broken wall, and stolen ore. It's not even a significant portion of the dwarves' iron anyway, just the ore that happens to be in two small, lightly-defended cities on the outskirts of dwarven territory.

This isn't anything that major at all, it just shows that lizardmen...
a) are capable of planned attacks
want iron
c) realize that there is no way in hell they can take on any army
d) want a war

Does anything else not make sense? I'll be happy to explain.

Edit: What do you mean this doesn't follow the plot?
Plot = kill villain.
Sargvaas = villain.
Gain by force of iron = reason to attack lizardmen and kill Sargvaas.
Now you know what do to, who to do it to, and a reason to do it.

He's making it for the benefit of the community, which apparently happens to have a lower intelligence than the likes of you.
One thing I've learned is that the actions that benefit or appeal to the moronic majority are far more appreciated than the actions that benefit a select minority. In this case, that minority is you, and maybe a few others.

I believe we've settled with "envy of Maximo" as the cause for Atramentis' outbursts. The belief that the three moderator's opinions are the most popular (Maximo's "c") has never been mentioned before Maximo posted it, and can safely be ruled out as a possible motivation.

Pardon the disorganization: the above is in response to the content below your numbered points. I'll respond to your numbered points next.

1. While prolific posting certainly doesn't mean arbitrarily that the opinion will be the most respected, it just so happens that a common quality of respected members is prolific posting. By recognizing the three mentioned as the most respected members (or givers of opinion, in case you raise an objection against this) as prolific posters, you're only helping to establish that their opinions will be more respected, though not necessarily saying that their opinions will be definitely respected.

2. I'm not sure entirely of Maximo's intended meaning, but I can respond in a more general sense. If a given opinion conflicts with three similar opinions by the three most respected members (your numbered response 2 as well assumes that these three "most respected members" exist, so don't try to tell me that I'm assuming they exist; I'm building off of what you have already established), we can easily see that the said opinion will be in the minority, especially considering that the "most respected" opinions are thus most likely because they are the most popular opinions, and therefore said opinion opens up its doors to the possibility of being irrational and/or false. It is always advisable to take minority opinions with a grain of salt. Let's take a look at a relevant example: Atramentis was in the definite minority when he rated Maximo's map a 0. The simple lack of explanation of the 0-rating immediately makes his reasoning assumed irrational. #44414 116 2005-01-04T21:38:33Z Tsukatu
Alright, screw the hidden text, I'm going to try to develop a unique scoring style. This time around, I'll include my general feel for the map before I grade in categories.

Map: Rooms 7
Author: Lartsa
Despite a clear lack of playtesting, and little focus on symmetry, this map is playable. Various problems, such as drones not doing what they're supposed to do (such as the drone that ends up doing stupid circles in the upper right chamber) and enemies that are bypassed way too easily (laser drones, chaingun drone), and a smattering of enemies that are nearly impossible to get past (the rocket launcher in the lower left), reared their ugly heads far too many times. As a map to play, it's quite entertaining. As a work of art, it isn't worth the load time.
Symmetry: 5; While the tileset and the room ideas were symmetrical, the general look of it didn't suggest much symmetry at all. I didn't feel I was doing anything similar in the two symmetrical portions, nor did I make any correlation between the symmetrical portions while playing.
Uniqueness: 7; Surprisingly, this kind of map is a rarity on NUMA, which is quite unfortunate. Seeing a level like this was a refreshment.
Fun: 8; I can't say it wasn't entertaining. Well, except for the lower-left rocket launcher.
Difficulty: 4; It tends toward being pretty damn easy, with a nice sudden spin into insane in the lower-left.
Excitement: 2; The general mood is relaxed. I didn't feel pressured by anything as I was playing the map.
Other: 1; Unoriginal name. If you want to be taken seriously in a competition, make up a better name.
Total: 27

Map: Circle of Death
Author: tktktk
More of artwork than a fun map to play, this map resembles more of a somewhat laidback test of coordination. Accessing the various switches can get tedious, however, and so it's much more appealing as a work of art.
Symmetry: 10; The thwumps at the top (that don't do anything) are enough like the floor guards at the bottom to truly make this map nearly perfectly symmetrical.
Uniqueness: 8; Maps like this have shown their faces on NUMA, and in one particular episode in the main game itself (the number escapes me), typically including the center of the map as a main focus, such as a "FL4M1NG SUN OF DEAHT!!1" or "TEH BIG FRICKIN EYE!1!"
Fun: 5; It doesn't seem like it, but this map is kind of boring to play. There is nothing to preoccupy you in your moving from one area to the next. It seems like you're moving freely to rooms that each contain their own separate challenge.
Difficulty: 7; Getting the four buttons on the sides can be frustrating, depending upon your method. The rest is pretty easy, up until you get to the exit, where it turns to dependency on luck.
Excitement: 1; Very laidback.
Other: 5; Working completion demo.
Total: 36

Map: A War At Tarawa
Author: JeR(K)
As exciting as it looks, and far more convoluted than it looks, this map presents a challenge to just about anyone bored enough to try it. The difficulty picks up toward the finale, containing surprisingly difficult situations. The end is rather lax, however, and nothing short of tedious.
Symmetry: 10; Aside from the doors, this map is perfectly symmetrical.
Uniqueness: 8; Gotta admit you don't see many of the "dick around below to access the top" maps.
Fun: 7; The bottom was pretty entertaining, but the top was just plain annoying in its difficulty.
Difficulty: 4; This was definitely unbalanced. The bottom was a snap - you could practically ignore the existence of the drones, and you'd do fine. The two side rooms on the top were crazy hard, and the top central room was pathetically easy.
Excitement: 3; The bottom can be exciting if you want to play around with the drones, but the top can never become exciting - you die too quickly, at a high frequency.
Other: 1; No demos suggest that there's a possibility you didn't playtest it, which is hinted at by the difficulty of the top corner rooms.
Total: 33

Map: Tentacles
Author: Igi
The radiation sign dubbed "tentacles" has a misleading appearance: the chaingun drones that make the map look like a goofy face belie the map's sadistic challenges.
Symmetry: 6; Symmetrical in two different ways that clash a bit. The sides would have been better filled in completely, and the opposite drone movements make the map look disorganized.
Uniqueness: 9; This is pretty unique. These maps aren't rare, but good maps like these are.
Fun: 7; Once you look past all of the death and agony, this is a fun map to play. Once.
Difficulty: 6; At times, it seems too difficult, but that's really just moderately challenging situations strung together.
Excitement: 5; All the way. You're never completely safe, and you have to keep moving to avoid death.
Other: 1; No... demos...
Total: 34

Map: Insert Palindromes Here
Author: Brickman
This map was surprisingly entertaining. It's an excellent example of how a map can be both art and fun to play... like an action movie with a good plot.
Symmetry: 10; Three cheers for symmetry!
Uniqueness: 9; The inside seems like something Maximo would do, and the tileset is verging on typical for a lot of maps, though it's not very evident.
Fun: 8; All except for getting the exit switch and the moving between areas under fire.
Difficulty: 8; Pretty appropriate for your average Joe N player.
Excitement: 3; You can pretty much ignore the four enemies in the top and bottom and continue doing your thing... they don't interfere much. The real excitement comes from jumping matrix-like to the corner switches and in timing your passage through the drones.
Other: 2; You played through your level twice, and didn't bother to record a demo? That and the name is boring.
Total: 40

I'm doing this at school, so I don't exactly have time. More later.

#45286 35 2005-01-10T03:20:06Z Tsukatu
:vomits again:
Ugh. Messy.

The car is doing nothing with its velocity. The velocity is indirectly causing the deer to disintegrate.

You can look at it two ways, they both work:
The convoluted way:
The velocity means that the car has to have a massive decelleration because it needs to come to a complete halt from a high speed in a very small timeframe. The decelleration, when factored in with the car's mass, gives you a force (F=ma). So basically, when the deer and the car hit, the car is slowed down extremely quickly, and that resulting slowing force is reflected onto the deer. For every force, there's an equal and opposite force, right? That's not always a push. The car's frame is pulled in towards itself, and the deer's carcass does the same thing, as an opposing force to the car's frame's deformative force.
The easy way:
Having a velocity means that the car has Kinetic energy. Energy is always conserved (unless there are some funky nuclear reactions going on, which there aren't in this incident). Let's take the car-road-deer system. However much energy those three have stored in them, that number stays constant (ignoring friction with the road and air). That means that when the car stops, it loses its kinetic energy... but the total energy of the system stays the same, so that energy has to go somewhere. In this case, it goes into the deformation of the car and the deer.

Velocity does not directly do anything besides say that the car is, in fact, moving. To change velocities, whether it be coming to a stop or speeding up, in any amount of time, you need an acceleration. And in this case, it's the acceleration (decelleration, to be exact) that's directly causing all of the damage.

Edit: Mispelled "deer."

Through the foggy ocean mists, the warships seemed to be coming from every direction. There was plenty of bustle atop the ships as they approached. It looked like the lizardmen were pulling the iron out of the boats that were roped to the larger boats and moving them to the larger boat, though it wasn't clear why. Then some lizards climbed into the now empty boats, taking some ropes with hooks on them, and began lowering themselves into the water...
Soon, rowboats and longboats covered the ocean as the larger ships turned around to escape with the ore they could, riding significantly lower in the water due to the added weight from the smaller ships' load of iron. In each rowboat were two lizards, both in full acoutrements, and in each longboat were four, similarly armed and armored. Working together, each pair was able to make surprising speed toward the closest of the six stolen vessels - the one containing Imir and Detario, along with the bound rogue Szarzina. When Detario, on the top deck, had regained his senses, there was a longboat and two rowboats twenty feet from Detario's hull. One among each boat stood up and began to twirl a grappling hook.
It seemed the lizards sent this force out to see if they could regain control of the boats that were stolen. If they succeeded, good for them, it means more iron ore. If they fail, they die. No support will be given to them, since no warship filled with iron will risk its iron to help out, especially since the Human navy was alerted.

#46079 10 2005-01-14T03:44:13Z Tsukatu
Not really a magic trick, and not really "squeezing" between anything, it's simply how the game copes with movement and massive velocities. When the ninja moves, instead of having the pixels he's made of physically haul bacon over to the new location, his previous position's pixels disappear, and then they reappear in the new position. He doesn't exist anywhere in between. The game does this so fast that you see it as fluid movement, but really, he's making like a Bohr electron and doing that funny cilantro trick where he can move from one place to another without ever actually being in between those two places!
So because the ninja is moving so damn fast, the space he travels in that split second is enough that the ninja exists in the open spaces on the way up. As far as the game is concerned, there are no tiles blocking the way, since it doesn't detect any solid tiles directly in the way of where the ninja is.

Map: Intact
Author: LittleViking001
Symmetry: 8; Some more usage of the rotational symmetry.
Uniqueness: 7; Long-distance minefield hopping! Yay!
Difficulty: 6 Too easy if you don't want to get all gold. If you do want to get all gold, it's a simple matter of guiding the rocket into one of the many available walls and waiting for the next before dodging toward another gold pile.
Fun: 5; Kinda tedious. And when you got up through the tediousness to the rocket areas, and you died accidentally, you had to go through more tediousness.
Exitement: 1; This was very laidback, especially without a time limit. I could take my damn sweet time on it, including the rocket areas.
Other: 5; Demo.
Total Score: 32

Map: Think, Stupid, Think!
Author: tktktk
Symmetry: 7; *sigh* Here we go again with one of the more boring forms of symmetry... vertically down the center. It was used well, though.
Uniqueness: 9; Much of the stuff you use here is pretty cool to look at / do, and I haven't seen it before. Good job.
Difficulty: 7; Working its way to kinda hard, but it's still challenging enough (without being frustratingly so) for newbies.
Fun: 7; Yay. Constant action, though it's still easy to avoid death.
Excitement: 3; The enemies were remarkably easy to avoid. The real excitement came when I had to figure out exactly how to get into the exit.
Other: 5; Demo.
Total Score: 38

Author: tktktk
Symmetry: 6; Looks kinda messy and it doesn't seem like certain parts work as smoothly when they're inverted due to reflection from symmetry.
Uniqueness: 9; Once again, tktktk refuses to abuse cliche concepts as so many mapmakers do today.

Fun: 6; Can't be much fun if it's too hard, especially in the messy close-quarters central area.

Other: 5; Demo.

At first, I thought you wanted to do object symmetry over the x-axis and tileset symmetry over the y-axis, but I was dissapointed.

Fun: 6; Yeah, I don't like running back and forth.

#47431 46 2005-01-23T04:35:08Z Tsukatu
Okay, simply for the few of us that can program in these languages, and for my benefit in case it happens again and my computer decides to be stupid, here are the things I used to fix the problem:

Typing this into the Run menu:
REG add HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v DisableRegistryTools /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

Putting this in a .reg file:
REGEDIT4

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\.exe]
@="exefile"
"Content Type"="application/x-msdownload"

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\exefile]
@="Application"
"EditFlags"=hex:d8,07,00,00

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\exefile\shell]
@=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\exefile\shell\open]
@=""
"EditFlags"=hex:00,00,00,00

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\exefile\shell\open\command]
@="\"%1\" %*"

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\exefile\shellex]

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\exefile\shellex\PropertySheetHandlers]

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\exefile\shellex\PropertySheetHandlers\{86F19A00-42A0-1069-A2E9-08002B30309D}]
@=""

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\exefile\DefaultIcon]
@="%1"

Putting this in a .vbs file:
'Enable/Disable Registry Editing tools
' Doug Knox - rev 12/06/99

Option Explicit

'Declare variables
Dim WSHShell, n, MyBox, p, t, mustboot, errnum, vers
Dim enab, disab, jobfunc, itemtype

Set WSHShell = WScript.CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
p = "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\"
p = p & "DisableRegistryTools"
itemtype = "REG_DWORD"
mustboot = "Log off and back on, or restart your pc to" & vbCR & "effect the changes"
enab = "ENABLED"
disab = "DISABLED"
jobfunc = "Registry Editing Tools are now "

'This section tries to read the registry key value. If not present an 
'error is generated. Normal error return should be 0 if value is 
'present
t = "Confirmation"
Err.Clear
On Error Resume Next
n = WSHShell.RegRead (p)
On Error Goto 0
errnum = Err.Number

if errnum <> 0 then
'Create the registry key value for DisableRegistryTools with value 0
WSHShell.RegWrite p, 0, itemtype
End If

'If the key is present, or was created, it is toggled
'Confirmations can be disabled by commenting out 
'the two MyBox lines below

If n = 0 Then
n = 1
WSHShell.RegWrite p, n, itemtype
Mybox = MsgBox(jobfunc & disab & vbCR & mustboot, 4096, t)
ElseIf n = 1 then
n = 0
WSHShell.RegWrite p, n, itemtype
Mybox = MsgBox(jobfunc & enab & vbCR & mustboot, 4096, t)
End If

Yep yeppers. 'Tis how 'twas done.

#47785 2 2005-01-24T18:55:48Z Tsukatu
I should think so, unless the problem is within your hard drive. For example, and this is using a Windows machine, actually...
One day my computer said to itself, "I think I'll delete crucial system files."
And it did.
I couldn't start Windows, and I was stuck in DOS. Because I know how to get around in DOS, I started looking for problems. Well, as it turned out, some system files weren't in their correct positions, and others were missing altogether. Actually, one wasn't being correctly read, despite its normal extension and correct folder placement.
So anyway, the rest of my hard drive was fine... I just needed some method of transfering it.
So basically, if you can figure out where exactly the problem is, you can (using DOS, Macs have that, right?) see if the rest of your hard drive is intact. Then what you do is put in a removable hard drive in addition to your old one, install it through DOS (quite possible, though sometimes frustrating), and then transfer all of your files, except for all that C:\Windows crap onto the removable hard drive. Then... buy a new computer. Or get your old one fixed by professionals. But sometimes it's cheaper to just buy a new one. Then just stick your removable into the new computer, and you're set.

#48421 26 2005-01-29T06:56:33Z Tsukatu
*sigh*
The site is stupid. It goes directly against excerpts from Newton's actual books, which I'm too tired to dig up right now.
It basically makes the mistake of calling "normal force" the "centrifugal force." The normal force is the force you get when you have an object being pushed into a surface, and the normal force is the surface pushing back. Where you're sitting right now, you have a gravitational force on your butt, and the chair gives back a normal force because of Newton's action-reactiong pair business.
So the normal force acts exactly as a centrifugal force would act if it existed. The main problem with calling it centrifugal is that it confuses people who think that the main force involved with simple harmonic motion (like the circular path) is an outward-pushing force, which is untrue. Calling it that would also be adding another force to the equation, since you will always have a normal force pushing back. If we're told there's a centrifugal force, then we think to ourselves, "here is the centripetal force, and the normal force counteracting it, and then the centrifugal force as well counteracting the centripetal force... so essentially we have any rotation immediately leaving its circular path because it has more of a pull to the center of the circle."

Let's say you have a bucket of water and you're swinging it around your head with your arm. The water is going to be pulled inward by a centripetal force, and so is the bucket. The problem is that the bucket is pushing against the water because it's also affected by the centripetal force, so the water pushes back and ends up going in a line tangent to the point on the circle it currently occupies. So what about the bucket then? Why doesn't it rocket toward the center of the circle, seeing as how we've only shown it has a centripetal force, and no surface to provide a normal force in opposition in the same way the bucket acted on the water? Well, your arm acts as a rope and provides a tension force that counteracts just that. So in the end, we have all of the forces cancel out, and the only thing that happens is that it gets a velocity on a path tangent to the point on the circle it occupies.

It's difficult to visualize, but that's one of the best known examples.

The theme is: "I hate Tsukatu!"
To clear some stuff up: this contest was not set up because of any depression-induced self-deprecating desires. I just felt that there should be a light-hearted contest, and I thought of an accompanying theme.
Note: You don't have to hate me in order to participate.
If anyone actually does hate me, then you can take it up with me privately.
In this circumstance, though, I'm just giving you guys a theme that has no relation to what you actually think of me.
So fire away!

This contest shows more focus on the artistic aspect of the map, so the gameplay categories aren't as significant.
You guys make maps, and they'll be judged according to the following categories:

Design: 10; How well does the map as a whole show your hate?
Creativity: 10; What kinds of new ideas are implemented?
[Judge Specified]: 10; That's right, it can be anything from "Effectiveness as a survival map" to "Is it a duck." This is for judges who feel that the map isn't being properly scored on the categories given.
Difficulty: 5; How well is the map scaled for beginners/veterans? Can the veterans expect a higher challenge if they want to all-gold the map?
Fun/Excitement: 5; I always thought this should be one category.
Demo: 5; Is there a demo? How good is it?
Other: 5; Anything else you want to add but couldn't in [Judge Specified].

The judges can also hand out 5 points to their favorite map, when their judging is finished.
Other than that, the rules for this contest will use the same ones as Maximo's string of Nedcons.

Any nominations for judges? I'll take two besides me, and one backup.

#49418 26 2005-02-06T03:00:29Z Tsukatu
Have you ever seen a melee attack in Halo? That's the best example of hitting someone with the butt of a weapon.

Try this if you can't picture how easy it is:
Put your hands up as if you were holding a rifle, with your left hand holding the barrel steady for aiming and your right hand holding the butt of the gun, with finger on the trigger. I think we can agree that it's easy to quickly remove your finger from the trigger and to drop the butt from your shoulder.
Do these two simultaneously, with a speed consistent with hitting someone:
-Arc your left hand either (1) up so that it is over your left shoulder or (2) left so that it's next to your left bicep.
-Arc your right hand either (1) underneath the gun, bringing the underside of the hilt into your enemy's face, or (2) right, making the butt hit your enemy in the side of his head.
Both examples use the point between your hands as a point of rotation, so that part of the gun pretty much remains in the same spot.
In both (1) and (2), the gun barrel never points at you, and only accidental discharge of the firearm is possible, since your finger needs to be off the trigger. It's also easy to put the gun right back up to aim.

#49937 17 2005-02-10T05:08:59Z Tsukatu
My point of view:
There's no way we can know for certain.
And like all things we cannot know for certain, we shouldn't care, because if we have no hope of knowing, we can't put it to good use aside from theoretical ramblings.

I could say that all of my actions can be determined through analyzing exactly what situations arise based on analysis of my and other people's minds and how they react in those situations. We could literally plot out my life, and we could develop a script that you could watch me play out for you. However, it would take horrible amounts of time and effort, and generally isn't worth it.

I could also just as well say that I don't care about predestination, because it's like a movie I haven't watched, and to watch it I need to act as if I had choice, so that (even though I don't have a choice), the actions derived from my belief that I have a choice will make for a unique movie. Those who say that they have no choice, and so might as well do nothing are condemning themselves to a bad movie. I, in acting as if I had a choice, can almost assure myself a good movie.

I could even say that human impulses and the striking of neurons is random enough that no situation can be predicted, and since predestination relies heavily (read: entirely) on divination, then it is useless when trying to predestine something that can't be figured to happen for sure.

I could also argue any of these to the death, but really, in the end, it doesn't matter. So what if we are predestined to do stuff? That doesn't mean we can figure out what that stuff is or that we should stop living or anything.

So I act (without knowing, nor caring) as if I had a choice. If predestination exists, then I'm looking forward to a good movie. If predestination doesn't exist, then I can carve myself a good life out of my own choice.

If we're talking about predestination, how's this:
Just about anything can be predicted, even though it may be very hard and time-consuming to predict. The motion of a ball can be predicted perfectly if done properly (considering fluctuation in wind, drag, particles in air, rotation of Earth, etc). Actions of a person can be predicted (not realistically, but theoretically possible) if you analyze the neurons in that person's brain. In the case of Shroedinger's Cat, you can examine the deteriorating substance and figure out where certain atoms will be based on the deterioration already in effect on individual quarks, and figure out how the particles will bounce off of each other, so that the half-life/poisonous gas thing will kick in. We have no means to do this kind of analysis, but if we did, it'd be possible to predict this stuff, right?

So if everything can be predicted, then there's a definite future that can't change.

Quote: Daddaluma, Feb 16 2005, 07:43 AM
If you had, you would have had it clearly explained to you by the ever charismatic captain Picard that it's impossible to accelerate to the speed of light. But if you instantly jump to a speed above it, then you've bypassed that whole sticky infinite mass problem.

Lay off the pot and get into a physics classroom now.

It's the other way around. It's very possible to accelerate "faster than" the speed of light (assuming that you mean nothing can accelerate faster than 3*10^8 m/s^2, which is stupid, as I explain below). Bullets do it all the time. Circus performers who get shot out of canons do it all the time as well. The only issue is that they have that acceleration for less than a second.

The speed of light, by the way, is 3 * 10^8 m/s, or 300,000,000 meters per second.

If you get a gun and know its muzzle velocity, and then know the time it takes for the bullet to leave the barrel (a fraction of a second), you'll see that dividing the two (m/s divided by s gives you m/s/s = m/s^2, which is acceleration) gives you a considerably high acceleration.

So if something travels at 500 bajillion m/s^2 for 100 bajillionths of a second, we get a speed of 5 m/s, which is not faster than the speed of light.

You can't even compare the speed of light and acceleration. Saying "an acceleration greater than the speed of light" or "accelerate faster than the speed of light" is a crime against physics. Velocity and acceleration cannot be directly compared without a time. It's like saying that something is bigger than purple. You simply can't compare the two. but if you add another variable (like time when comparing an acceleration and a velocity) such as a maximum size purple objects can be, then you can compare the two. You can call an object bigger than an object that is purple.

Do you know what the clipboard is? It's part of any Windows OS. It's what you copy stuff to. When you select text or images or something and you "copy" or "cut" it, that text/image is stored on the clipboard. Pasting takes the data from the clipboard and puts it wherever you're pasting it.
So copying a level to the clipboard means that you've effectively selected the level data and copied it. All you need to do is open some text editor (preferably notepad) and paste. Yay! Then you save the file.

For those of you who have and use Steam, get The Specialists. When I first saw it, I said to myself, "wow, this looks like everything I've ever wanted in a FPS."

Then I actually played it. After joining the first server, I couldn't pick my jaw up off of the floor. You can bet the next four words out of my mouth were "oh em f cking gee."

I suggest you get the game, don't read up on anything or view any demos... but instead head straight into a deathmatch game with lots of players, go spectator, and just watch. I absolutely guarantee you you'll be completely blown away.

The very first thing that happened with me:
I read the manual and saw all the really cool stuff you could do. So I set up my own server where I could practice this awesome stuff. After I got a loose grip on the controls and the nifty matrix-ey moves, I joined a deathmatch server.
The very first thing I saw when I walked through the doors of dm_corporate was some black dude in a trench coat and sunglasses doing a sideways no-hands cartwheel past the doorway... time slowed down (bullet-time), and he opened fire on me with two uzis. I got shot a whole helluva bunch, then ran after him with my shotgun. Some other guy decides to party, too, but uzi-man does a flip over me (jumping completely out of the way of my shotgun blast) and kicks the other dude in the face. I whip around and try to shoot him again, but he jumps away again to the side, and I miss him by miles. As for my third (and final) shot, he was running toward a wall, and I led, but he did a backflip thingy off the wall and shot me again.
So I died, but it was so friggin' awesome. I had to pause to get a shovel and a wheelbarrow to unload the steaming piles of awesome from my room, disconnecting from the server to stop the merciless flood of red-hot awesome.

As the title says, I have never been so impressed with a FPS. This game is cooler than three times Halo and Halo 2 combined, after mixing in a pinch of Half-Life 2. I am not kidding you.

Why the hell are you still reading this? Download it, sucka!

#52145 8 2005-03-01T22:25:04Z Tsukatu
Here's one that's completely crystal clear... with no "fraction of a second" business. This took me twenty or so minutes to get consistently:

-Make sure that as you start the level, you're holding down the "move left" key.
-As you approach the end of the first ledge, keep holding down left, and press and hold jump, too, so that your jump is redirected in the top left corner to go downward faster. You should land on the first thwump.
-As the thwump leaves and you're standing on air, hold down "right," so that you end up standing on top of the second thwump (and it's passing by very quickly).
-As you fall from that thwump (you should be right up against the right wall), do a wall-jump just above the niche below, and end up standing on top of the thwump as it recedes back to its hiding spot. Make sure to go back to the right in mid-wall jump, so that you end up next to the same bit of wall from which you launched.
-You should at this point be right up against the right wall, standing on top of the last thwump as it moves slowly backwards. At this point, don't do anything. Just let yourself fall from the thwump, slide down the ramp thing, and you'll fly past the drone and land on the ground below.
-As soon as you hit the ground, start running right, to continue with the level.

That's me totally overexplaining it, anyway. Any chance to fail this should be eliminated with the standing on the thwumps, which are more or less an occurance independent of your actions

#53027 24 2005-03-07T08:54:48Z Tsukatu
I have a problem with being half-asleep, actually. People tell me it's entertaining, but this only adds to... previous experience... enough that I can most definitely testify that without a doubt I know what it is like to be delightfully mad.
It's all about being really, really tired, and then passing out, and then having someone wake you up right when you're about to go unconscious (of course, my window is friggin' massive, so it happens more than I'd like it to).

It's a crazy feeling (haha)... you think exactly as you think now, just as consciously, except that your reasoning is horribly askew. Everything you say makes perfect sense to you, as if you were perfectly conscious and sane having a normal discussion... but stuff everyone else says tends to be off-kilter. If they're trying to demonstrate something to you, it won't make sense, and they'll be so blindly stupid that you just have to argue. And your arguments all make perfect sense, while theirs are completely illogical (and then when you snap out of it, you realize how wrong you are). I've done messed up stuff when half asleep.
The worst, though, is when you're deprived of sleep and you start hallucinating. When I got my very first job working at a pizza place, the very following night was filled with me being half asleep and taking orders from people who weren't there. I've gotten up out of bed physically to run into a hallway and have a one-sided conversation with someone. I've ordered pizza, too.
Other fun stuff includes the time I got out of bed and was convinced that life was CounterStrike. So I bought an m4 and snuck out of bed. I even saw a friggin' crosshair. In the shower, I tried to convince myself that it wasn't real... but, and this is the worst part about it all, you also reason irrationally that you have no time to think about how logical stuff is, and you end up in a panic because you don't have time to analyze the situation. I failed in trying to convince myself. I was still very wary of terrorists when I snuck upstairs to eat breakfast. Then I fell asleep on the couch, and then woke up, and was perfectly fine, wondering why the hell I was on the couch and holding my paintball gun.
Oh, and most recently, I realized in the shower that I am not, in fact, an angel.

Don't talk to me in the morning. I will most likely be talking to people who don't exist about something completely irrational.

#2615 1 2005-04-21T17:54:04Z Tsukatu
Here it is. I should tell you that I had a size limit on this thing, so I didn't get in all that I wanted to get in:

Quote: My Beef With Theism
If I were forced to pick one thing in the world that I despise, Id have to say its religion. Nothing makes me feel sorry for and dislike the world as much as religion. It wasnt always this way. I remember a time when I was deeply religious and thought that religion was the best thing for someone. Then I turned nine.
I was once Russian Orthodox. I was very devoted to my faith. I would pray every night, I would talk to God, and I would credit Him for making me as great as I was (I thought very highly of myself in my younger years). But as I grew older, I began to question my faith. Was it really God that was making my life blissful, or was it simply that the circumstances of my life naturally and conveniently made me happy? As soon as I realized that happiness can come from something besides God, I was torn between atheism and theism.
To solve this problem, I decided to look into proving God. It was just about as hard as it sounds. The evidence I saw for God was the fact that the majority of the world believed in Him and that the Bible affirms his existence. I tried to look at the Bible first, but ended up dropping the pursuit, mainly because I couldnt read Slavic (and the Bible was written in Slavic in my church) and because I didnt have the patience. So instead, I compared general majority opinion and the general agreement that God exists.
Now, I think abstractly (relative to the majority of the world, which thinks concretely), and its very easy for me to prove something to myself definitely in a short amount of time. For most of the year, when everyone else in my second grade class was swinging on the monkey bars or going down the slide repeatedly, I was sitting on the corner of the sandbox thinking about God. By the end of that year, I had absolutely no doubt in my mind that God was about as real as Santa Claus or the Tooth Fairy. From what I remember (which isnt much), it was a lengthy series of conditional ad absurdum arguments about God, combined with the fact that a positive assertion (like a theory) needed clear proof to be taken seriously, that made his existence entirely impossible.
When the day came that I made the definite conclusion that God did not exist, I was very concerned that I might be wrong and that God would hate me or something, but as time went on, my growing wisdom only provided me more affirmation that God does not exist. And so I went into third grade a proud atheist. I had no problem with others believing. I just assumed that their parents would tell them what I believed to be the truth or that the kids would figure it out for themselves. It didnt surprise me that I was the only one to realize this truth, since I went to a public school and was consistently at the top of my class.
My alarm at the blind faith of the world grew substantially when I went to a religious private school, realizing that the school was created by adults that believed in God. To me, this was just the same as an adult that believed in the Easter Bunny. The masses that I had to sit through, all part of going to a Catholic school, made me realize that this was a serious issue and that people actually believed what I considered to be baloney. It was also most likely what made me think less of theists intellectually.
As I moved on, my beliefs became an excellent candidate for the most influential force in my life. As I picked up odd bits of wisdom with age, my atheism was being constantly reaffirmed in new ways, from completely different angles. By the time I reached 8th grade, I had denounced the Bible as the worst crime on human integrity in the history of man. Worse yet, which made me sick to my stomach the moment I realized it, people in the world took it literally without any qualms or second doubts.
At one point in my life (its hard to pin down), I also realized that there are other religions aside from Christianity. I looked into them with interest, but rolled my eyes when I saw that most of these religions contained god figures. Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism, theyre all the same to me. They all believe in inconsistent gods that have no hope of existing. I stopped caring about nuances between them. I dont care whether God/Elohim/Allah/Brahma tells us to eat red meat or not, its still some god figure trying to direct human lives for absolutely no reason. Buddhism and Zen stood out in this crowd, however, since they believed in balances of forces rather than god figures, but I ended up turning my head from them as well when I realized they came from human need to explain something and in his haste forgetting to apply reasoning, instead relying on the fact that things that sound mystical and super-neato are mistaken (even by themselves) as some ultimate wisdom. To me, it was all about the phrase, gee, wouldnt it be cool if...
But what really gets me going about religion is that even those masses that I consider brainwashed and inferior dont act consistently with their beliefs. Jesus taught Christians to turn the other cheek and to love their enemies, right? God wants peace, and Christianity promotes peace and benevolence, right? Youd think so, because clergymen and the Bible and any Christian will tell you that a Christian ought to be kind and merciful and peaceful and loving. This is pounded and etched into the skulls of any Christian. If this is all true, why is a Christian 40 times more likely (statistically, based on prison censuses) than an atheist to commit a violent crime, such as murder or serial rape? Quote: Nothing But Common Sense
I think positively of myself. Some may call it an ego, some may go as far as calling it narcissism, but the majority calls it elitism. Im ambitious and very optimistic about my future. I have high standards for myself and have unwavering confidence in my intellectual abilities.
Because I see such value in the integrity of my mind, I have sworn... eternal hostility against every form of tyranny over the mind of man (Thomas Jefferson). My mental acuity defines me. Without it, I am nothing. For this reason, I see absolutely nothing beneficial coming from anything that causes damage to my mind, be it in the form of impairment of judgment, obsession/addiction, or physical damage.
This vendetta upon such forms of tyranny really began with my dislike of religion. Through all of my experience with religion, I have realized the importance of soundness of mind. I saw religion as retarding perception and retarding objective analytical ability. I refused to adopt religion because I felt it would do this to me, limiting my cognitive ability. I wouldnt stand for it.
But this lesson learned applied to much more than religion. When I was very young, I would see my parents drinking alcohol casually and wanted to do the same, to be like them. They would never let me have a drink (understandably), and I thought it was unfair. But after my series of revelations about the impact of religion on the mind and the importance mental integrity, as well as the discovery of what alcohol does to the mind, my perspective changed drastically. When my mother offered me a glass of wine on my 16th birthday, I responded with a cold stare and an explanation that offering me a glass of anything alcoholic was going to be received as an offer to remove one of my limbs.
People tell me I overreact to these things, but I disagree. Alcohol, for example, gives you an addiction, helps you lead a false life (the loosening-up effect of alcohol), associates you with a statistically more violent and ignorant crowd, destroys your intellect, and drastically ups your chances of dying on any given night. What are the benefits? It tastes good? I am utterly astounded that bars exist, but clubs in which patrons serve knives with which customers can stab themselves in the leg do not. The same goes for any kind of narcotic and for tobacco.
But what about the benefits of, for example, wine? It helps prevent heart disease, right? Two words: grape juice. I especially despise wine, mostly because it comes with all of the negatives of any other kind of alcoholic drink, except that its also ridiculously expensive and that its had far more hype than it deserves (which would be none). Wine connoisseurs just tick me off. Grape juice tastes better, is far cheaper, easier to get, legal for minors (teaching by example is a good thing), and better for your heart than wine.
Its really nothing but common sense. You can either pay more and risk your life, well-being, social happiness, intelligence, and success in life with some minor benefits, or you can have those same benefits, but greater, and without any of the downsides. It really comes down to, do you want to be stupid, or do you not want to be stupid?
My dislike of these things, I believe, came directly from my experiences with religion, which is simply further evidence for me that my religious beliefs are the most influential forces on my life.

I can explain the cheesiness of that last paragraph. The essay was really about a value I hold and how I got that value, and I wanted to show how much influence my antitheism has had on me. I realized at the end that the paper had little to nothing to do with religion, so I stuck in a corny concluding paragraph that I was considering revising.

One such group worshipped a god named, in Latin, Lucifer. He was the bringer of light (as his name suggests), and he was a benevolent god who helped mortals see the truth by casting his light in shadowy areas. It was usually Lucifer that this group talked about when they were discussing conversions ("let Lucifer shine his light for you, and you'll see that ours is the true way"). So naturally, them Christians wanted to foul up his name. They told people that Lucifer is not the bringer of truth, but instead the Prince of Lies. Yeah, that's it, and the only person who would want to lie to you like that would be Satan, with the intent to steer you from God's grace! Don't be swayed! Hold fast in your beliefs!
So why is it Satanism, a synonym for what would be Luciferism? Well, my theory is that, for shits and giggles, the guy who came up with Satanism wanted a name with some shock-value to it, and Satanism just sounded cooler.
Calling it Satanism is just calling it the fact of the matter. It has absolutely no connection to Satan, and especially not the Christian Satan. It's just a word that Christians (who make up a majority of the world) relate to, so they can clearly identify that Satanists opposed them directly. What better way to tell someone you are opposed to everything they believe in?

#3292 1 2005-06-13T04:58:54Z Tsukatu
I was talking to one of my friends about marijuana the other day when I realized that I didn't know very much about it. What I get from him (and I don't know that this is true, but I do trust him) is that marijuana doesn't cause any permanent damage.

So from what I gather...
Marijuana alters your way of thinking, opening up parts of your brain you wouldn't normally use, and makes you see things from completely different angles. This effect is completely temporary, and there is no harm to your mind or rest of your body (more on this a little later). That is, you get that high, but when it's over there isn't any damage whatsoever, just some neurons that connected to parts of your brain that they didn't connect to before - not necessarily bad. You can avoid damage to your lungs by obtaining marijuana in pill form, and using it in moderation (very easy to do) removes chance of addiction. So basically, it's a positive effect without any negatives.

Of course, the main problems I still see with it are:
-Because it's illegal, and most Americans happen to be goody-two-shoes when it comes to drug laws, it's a pain in the ass to obtain, and you'll probably start being associated with some pretty sneaky people.
-Because it's illegal, you have to avoid authorities and parents. It doesn't seem worth the risk of being caught and fined or caught and disowned just to get that high. Plus, that makes it look addictive.
-While you are high, your sense of judgment can be much different (not necessarily impaired, but it very well can be), and you risk doing some pretty stupid stuff when you're high. So you'd have to be in solitude in a padded room in a straitjacket while you're high if you want to eliminate the risk of dying/doing something retarded/injuring yourself severely accidentally. And also, while high, you are a less productive individual.

But then again, two of those can immediately be eliminated with legalization of marijuana, which leaves only that last one, which isn't even that big of a problem. More people (percentage-wise, making it comparable) crash when sleepy than when they are under the influence of marijuana, which makes the case that it doesn't impact your judgment to a great degree in the slightest - no more than being sleepy, anyway. So if there is a benefit, and legalization takes away most of the cons, and the last one remaining isn't even significant... what's so wrong with marijuana? I'd appreciate statistics.

Note: This is not to say that I do marijuana or ever will. In fact, I don't do marijuana, and in all likelihood, I never will. This is just for information purposes.

I just made the statement a little more general by tossing in the eating of fatty foods so that it would apply to more than just wine, which it does.

On top of that, I think you're very misinformed about how your body heals damage to itself. Let's use this foreign object you labeled a "knife." When you cut yourself with this "knife," you do damage to your skin tissue, and maybe even destroy the lining of one of your veins. Your body has a certain amount of energy, and it uses small portions of that energy (divided up) to carry out routine maintenance and growth functions. Let's say your body uses 100 AEUs (arbitrary energy units) in an hour. Whereas you could spend a few AEUs to create another layer of stomach lining, or a few dozen to grow some fraction of a millimeter, or maybe a dozen or so to create a fresh wave of red blood cells to replace old nasty ones, that energy is instead spent repairing your body. More damage means more of those AEUs are going to go toward repairing your body than adding to it. So if you were absolutely damage-less, 100 AEUs would go toward your improvement, building some muscle, helping you grow, stuff like that. If you receive a knife cut, 40 AEUs are going to go into repairing that cut, which leaves you with only 60 AEUs to improve yourself. If you drink, which does stuff like thins your blood and damages your mind and internal organs, your body is going to flip out when it sees that all 100 AEUs are needed to fix all the harm you're doing yourself, and even that won't be enough.

Now, you mention that if someone wants to be healthy that they must follow a very strict procedure. That is true, but only if you want to be perfectly healthy. This would include filtering the air you breathe and electromagnetically ensuring that your skin cells do not fly off of your body. Even though we don't go to these excessive means to stay healthy, it is recommended that we do our best to practical limits. So even though we eat foods that aren't perfectly in balance with the exact amount of nutrition we require for any particular meal, the damage that we receive from this is so miniscule that it hardly matters. It's a tiny fraction of an AEU. But there are other activities such as smoking and drinking that do relatively colossal damage to ourselves, and that is what sucks up our resources otherwise used for growth and improvement. Even when you use these in moderation, all you're doing is effectively punching yourself in the kidneys every few days.

There is no amount of alcohol small enough, even when used "in moderation," that does no damage to your system. All damage is permanent damage because the energy spent to repair it is permanently gone. Alcohol, when mixed with your blood, does harmful things. Period. That's by-the-atom. That's what alcohol does. You make it sound like the alcohol in your circulatory system sits and waits around for more of it to come along because it requires a large amount to do any damage, and then that drinking in moderation means that you never let the amount of alcohol in your body get large enough for it to do that damage. No no, that alcohol doesn't sit around in your blood saying, "c'mon, we just need a few more mils, and then we can start inflating this guy's liver!" This is comparable to America needing a certain amount of soldiers in Iraq for any one of them to start shooting something.

Whereas an atheist would say, "God does not exist," an antitheist would say, "God does not exist, and you're a dumbass if you think He does," and then add some ramblings about the negative influence theism has had on the world and individual.
Humanism is a philosophy... like a way to live your life. It's a lifestyle. A humanist indulges himself in pleasures of the flesh. He believes in the power of the individual. More on this a little later.
Satanism = Antitheism particularly geared against Christianity + Humanism + a pinch of religious fervor.

Main points:
-To a Satanist, Christianity is absolutely the dumbest thing anyone could possibly hope to invent or follow. It's absurd from its roots to its present condition, and anyone who follows is, simply put, scum. It's not a class issue, it's an intellectual issue.
-There ain't no Heaven, and there ain't no Hell, so have your fun while you're alive.
-The phrase "indulge on pleasures of the flesh" sounds grossly misleading, of course, so here's a better way of putting it: Do what makes you happy, as long as your pleasure doesn't cause anyone any excessive amount of direct or indirect harm. For most people, making other people happy makes them happy, so Satanists are typically among the more generous and friendly. Most people have more fun with friends, and have fun making friends, so Satanists are encouraged to be polite and respectful.
-Remember what Jesus said? "If someone strike thee on one cheek, turn the other like a dumbass?" Fuck Jesus, try "if someone strikes thee on one cheek, smash him on the other." Satanism uses its own version of the Golden Rule: "At the first encounter, treat others how you want to be treated. From that point on, treat them how they treat you." If you start out friendly and they respond with friendliness (i.e. you're both Satanists), then you're better off. But if you start out friendly and they act like a dick, then you shouldn't waste your time with them, and you've successfully avoided a stupid problem that'd only grow if you would've remained nice like a dumbass Christian.
-Christianity preaches abstinence, promising a better life after death. Isn't that just retarded though? Ignoring your natural urges only leads to your discomfort and your frustration, turning you into a prudish nazi homophobe racist. You should follow through with your uges (provided they don't harm anyone, as mentioned above) because they will all leave you happy, and you'll feel free and open, and like the world is yours for the taking. You'll feel absolutely great.
-Why the fuck would you ever be a prude? I mean seriously, what the fuck? You're denying yourself a whole world of potential pleasures if you fight your natural urges. That and being shy. Fuck being shy, that shit sucks. You don't enjoy anything if you're shy.
-Worship Satan. Make him happy. Satan is the only one who will give you pleasure, and God will give you nothing but pain and misery. "But," you ask, "how do you worship Satan when you insist that the story of God is a crock of shit?" Well that's easy. Are you ready for the answer? You ready for it? Really? Well, children, that Satan that you're being told to worship... is you. Yep, you're a god, dude. You = the Satan you're supposed to worship. You're the one that matters most to you. Make you happy.
-The three parts of Satanism are antitheism, because of the direct opposition against Christianity, humanism, because of the belief that the individual is the most important in existence, and a touch of religious fervor, because without zeal, you wouldn't have the motivation to improve yourself to be awesome. Think about it, people promise to work out and quit smoking and junk on their own terms, but they never go through with it because they only have intellectual motivation. But once you accept Satanism intellectually, you can freely "lose yourself" in Satanism in a way that can only be described as "religiously." You think crusaders would do what they did historically if it weren't for religious motivation? Well, use that same religious motivation to improve yourself so that you're more able to enjoy life.
-The majority of the world is Satanist without knowing it. All they're missing is the recognition that Christianity is stupid.
-Satanism encourages "evil" acts. Why does it encourage "evil" acts? Well, the Church, being ever so popular among the masses of idiots, defined most of the terminology used by people. So when they saw Satanism rear its glorious head, they feared it, and quickly unleashed propaganda about it calling everything they believe to be "evil." So if stuff we do, like make lots of friends and have fun with little to no inconvenience to people around us, is recognized as "evil" by the vast majority, we'll call it that, too, so it's easier to identify.

Why is it called Satanism, though? Why couldn't it be called something nicer?
For three reasons, as I see it:
-Satanism idealizes the (fictional) Christian anti-hero, Lucifer, known later as Satan. This (fictional) character is the epitome of the fight against oppression and restriction (God, another character in the same fictional story). Satan was totally fuckin' hot, and he revelled in it (ain't no reason to cover up your hotness). Satan didn't feel like being oppressed by that "God" asshole, so he fought for his freedom. And even though this isn't part of Satanic beliefs, it's my personal belief that he won that battle against God, because he got the better side of human nature, while God was stuck with the shithole that was abstinence, repression, and subjugation, basically anything that kills your self-esteem and keeps it down.
-A title like "Satanism" shows its clear opposition to Christianity.
-Satanism wouldn't be noticed if it weren't for the shock value. The name has done much more to attract the attention, the curiosity, and ultimately converts to Satanism.

That's about it. If you really want more on doctrine, read the first two books (and first two books only) of the Satanic Bible. If you read more than the first two books, I can guarantee you that you'll be thrown off by the content of the second books. He could've already, I'm just too lazy to check all over the goddamned place to find any traces of it. Anyway, it's been fun and very time-consuming. I might come back, but don't bet on it or hold your breath or anything. I have enough to fool around with these days, with no less than 7 girls I'm juggling in my mind who all quite clearly want me and a computer with four operating systems (DOS, Windows 98, Windows XP Home, and Slackware Linux).

I guess I'll have to leave with some kind of powerful quote or something...
...how about if I try to put down the philosophy that has made me the master of my social life ever since I discovered it a few years ago? That should do it.
Here's the idea:
Think of any situation that would cause any slight amount of panic or hesitation for you. It could be things like a friend of yours saying something strange or out of the ordinary, a girl you don't normally talk to flirting with you, things like that. The point is that there are so goddamned many of them. Then consider how much of your overall ability to do just about anything in those situations is limited by your hesitation, if not obliterated outright. Your thinking, judgment, and capacity for rational thought is shot completely. This is the initial realization, and it's pretty important. It's much deeper than I can say in words... meditate on it or something. And no, if you think you have it, you don't. Keep thinking. I'm serious.
Once you've accepted this and understood how huge of an impact it has in any social situation, there are two things you should do. Both take plenty of practice and focus, but they're most definitely worth it:
-Don't give in to hesitation. You can call it a zen thing if you want, but it really involves refusing to think. Panic and hesitation only comes when you fully grasp how odd and/or huge the situation is and how fucked you are if you don't do things perfectly, and the limitations to your ability to act and your mental faculties are only an issue because your mind considers the situation so important that it won't let the fact that you're totally frickin' screwed escape your head, and because that's all that remains in your mind, you don't have much room to do anything else. It's hard to explain, but you'll get what I mean if you just reread this a few times slowly, if you didn't on the first go. When something surprises you, force your mouth to open and say something, and refuse to think about the situation. It's very hard, and I guarantee you you'll get some pretty retarded results when you first try, but it's worth it in the end. For example, someone who doesn't refuse to assess the situation would stare at an attractive girl that just came up to talk to him with his jaw slack, his mind only on the idea "omfg this girl is totally fucking talking to me, I can't screw this up!" But someone who does refuse to assess the situation will force his mind to think nothing of it and act without hesitation. Once you eliminate hesitation, you remove by far the largest drawback anyone can have in a social situation.
-Use hesitation to your advantage impulsively. Another great way to put it (which I only found randomly a few weeks ago) is a quote that is somehow tied to Darth Maul - "Fear is my ally." This is extremely tricky to master (I hope to get that good some day). When you talk to people, be direct and keep them on their toes all the time. Represented physically, it'd be you pushing the person you're talking to backwards to the point where they have to move back or fall on their ass. Be courteous, of course, with plenty of intense eye contact. I found that 100% of the time (and I've been conducting this social experiment for a little over two years now), your friends will revere you and immediately consider you the best leader and wisest thinker they know, your enemies (if you're nice) will become laughably submissive, and girls will more often than not subconsciously confuse their panic and hesitation (all induced by you) for romantic feelings, and so you get some added fun there, too. But what is it you can do to keep people hesitating like this? Well, it's very easy if you have an active and powerful imagination (but especially if you have acting skills), though you're fucked if you don't. The reason this is so hard is because you have to follow multiple thought patterns in any given conversation. Not only are you thinking about your side of the conversation, but you're also thinking what the other person is thinking and analyzing what kinds of things you could say to knock them off balance, while still making sure nothing knocks you off balance. The one general strategy I can give you is this: make it so that the end of your sentence fills their head with simultaneous thoughts, most of which will induce some kind of panic or hesitation individually.
For example, let's say you're having a casual talk with a friend of yours and out of nowhere he starts lying to you about something. It would be stupid to try to cleverly trap him by proving that parts of his story couldn't work out, because that will make him focus primarily on inventing a story even though it will make him start to panic a little. A better way would be to keep looking straight into his eyes as you pause after hearing his response, then say something like, "alright, I'm going to ask you again, and this time I'd appreciate it if you didn't lie to me. What blah blah blah?" Yes, it does sound like you're interrogating them, but think of it this way - if you were in that position and you told what you thought was a convenient lie and he starts slowly doubting you, you could manage to uphold the story by adding things and leaving things ambiguous, etc.; but if you were asked politely to stop lying, you'd turn red instantly, and you'll receive all sorts of lingering and panic-inducing thoughts like, "oh shit, he knows I'm lying," "for future reference, it's a bad idea to lie to this guy," "I don't want him to get angry at me," "I hope he's not angry right now," and "I wasn't very nice to lie to him, was I?" All sorts of these will strike all at the same time, and the first words out of your mouth if you're hit with that rush of panic will be something like "uhhh... um.... uh..." And think about it - you'd consider that person influential and intelligent, and it'd feel more like you have to earn his respect (which people constantly strive for).

Anyway, if you don't get the idea, then either you don't deserve to know it or I'm bad at explaining these things.

Mac is free from viruses for the most part for one main reason. This may not sound like a serious reason, but believe me it's perfectly legitimate. I happen to have personal experience in this matter.

When making some kind of underhanded program, the most commonly targeted OS is Windows because the majority of the world uses it. You may notice that viruses are woefully unsuccessful when trying to attack a Linux machine, mostly because anyone who runs Linux in the first place knows enough about what they're doing that they can kill off the virus before anything bad happens. But no one makes a virus for a Mac because no one important uses a Mac. Big businesses usually use Linux or Windows, never Macs, so there's really no motivation to make viruses for Macs.
Now, if Macs were as popular as Windows, I bet you the opposite would be the case - Macs would have virus problems of epic proportions (because everyone is interested in making viruses for that OS) while we'd have some prepubescent jackass on Metanet called WindowsAddict_17 proclaiming that Windows doesn't have virus problems.

#128584 56 2005-12-30T23:26:59Z Tsukatu
To add more fuel to the fire, the author of the books "Snowcrash" and "Cryptonomicon" (I don't remember his name) wrote an essay once comparing the available OS's.

Paraphrased:
We can look at different operating systems as cars.
A Windows car is a pile of many, many pieces that all build and work off of each other. The result is very shaky, but it somehow manages to work. However, when there is a problem, it's very easy to locate the one problem part and replace it with a very small (if non-existent) fee.
A Mac car is a hermitically-sealed bubble. It's difficult to go on more "freestyle" roads with it, because it was built for efficient work. If something does go wrong with the car, because it's one big piece, the whole sonofabitch has to be replaced.
A Linux car is a tank. I don't mean one of those crappy soviet tanks, I mean something along the lines of a perfectly built (Swiss or German?) hovertank. It's extremely difficult to get it to break down. But what happens when it does break down? Eat three more metaphors:
Getting help with Windows isn't usually that big of a problem. The official Microsoft auto parts dealer is very nice about providing any replacement parts you need, usually at no charge. Sometimes you need to talk to a specialist, who are usually well-trained.
Getting help with a Mac isn't really getting help fixing as much as it is buying a new one.
Now, imagine a world where everybody loves tanks. The guy who invented a tank shared his design openly with the world, and since then an enormous community of tank-lovers and experts emerged, many of them even building their own tanks by fundamentally changing the design of the tank. There are millions of people in the world who know pretty much everything there is to know about a tank. Getting help with Linux is simply going online and finding one of the countless tech help forums that have a "Linux" subforum and asking. Usually anyone there will be able to tell you how to fix it and how to avoid having it happen again, and it's absolutely no cost to you!
We've compared design and repair. Now we'll cover economics.
100 people walk into a massive lot that contains Windows, Mac, and Linux vehicles. 90 of these people are attracted to the shininess and sleek facade of Windows, so they immediately get the impression that Windows is the best designed system. They pay the hefty price of a Windows vehicle, and buy many more Windows applications. 5 of these people are more attracted to Macs, for whatever retarded reason, and they decide to buy a Mac. But only 5 of the initial 100 people decide to walk over to the lot with the massive sign that says "FREE TANKS! GET YOUR TANK HERE! ANY DESIGN YOU WANT, WITH 100% CUSTOMIZABILITY! FREE TECH SUPPORT UNTIL THE END OF TIME! EFFECTIVELY AN UNLIMITED TIME WARRANTY!"

Fuck Macs.
Go Linux.
